contract.settlement_definition: KXATPWTA is now filed here and has rules text: 'If Alexander Zverev and Iga Swiatek win the 2027 Australian Open professional men's and women's singles tennis tournaments, then the market resolves to Yes'. Each market is a named pairing of one man and one woman at the same major; Yes requires both titles. 'If either participant forfeits, withdraws from consideration, or takes any official action that removes them from being able to win both ... the market will resolve to No for that pairing', so a withdrawal is a No, not a void. The pairing dies as soon as either player loses, and after one title is won it equals the other leg's marginal. Not stated: the source of truth, and whether other combination types (same player at two events) will be listed.

rules_evidence.quote: If Alexander Zverev and Iga Swiatek win the 2027 Australian Open professional men's and women's singles tennis tournaments, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The live combination is a men's-plus-women's pairing at one event: two different players in two separate draws, not the same player across two events.

rules_evidence.quote: If either participant forfeits, withdraws from consideration, or takes any official action that removes them from being able to win both
rules_evidence.establishes: A withdrawal or removal of either leg's player settles the pairing No, not void or fair price.

variants_and_edge_cases: Live structure (KXATPWTA): one man and one woman at the same major, in separate draws, so the legs are nearly independent; the joint is close to the product of the two title probabilities, with only shared-event conditions (heat policy, court pace, ball, scheduling disruption) as a weak positive link.
Withdrawal: per the rules any removal of either participant settles No for that pairing, so each leg's pre-draw withdrawal hazard enters directly as a No probability.
Leg resolution order: once one leg fails the pairing is dead; once one leg wins the pairing equals the remaining leg, so the price must be updated by conditional probability, not by marginals.
Other readings: same-player sequential combos (two majors) or two players in the same draw (mutually exclusive) are not listed; the same-player inputs here are conditional context only.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official tournament results of the named major's men's and women's singles; not named in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: The live combination (KXATPWTA) pairs a named man and a named woman to both win the same major, so its probability is the intersection of two title events in separate draws. Those legs are close to independent: the only shared channels are event-level conditions (court pace, heat and roof policy, scheduling disruption) that move both draws' favourites weakly in the same direction, so the joint is essentially the product of the two marginal title probabilities, each a path product over a seven-round draw that also carries the leg player's withdrawal hazard (a withdrawal settles the pairing No). For other combination readings that are not currently listed, dependence would come from three channels. First, a shared latent strength: a player who is truly better on a surface is better on similar surfaces, which makes consecutive titles positively correlated in a way that depends on the covariance between surface ratings. Second, a shared health and availability state that persists from event to event: an injury that removes a player from one leg removes him from the next. Third, event-to-event load: winning one tournament costs matches and recovery before the next, which creates a negative correlation in some calendars, and a mutual-exclusion structure when legs name different players at the same event. A simple product of marginals misses all of these, and a joint simulation with a shared player state is needed. The contract structure adds a path-dependence: as legs resolve, the combination collapses to a conditional probability.

stages.name: Leg definition and mutual-exclusion structure
stages.description: Required first: the rules text identifies the legs. KXATPWTA names one man and one woman at the same major, so the live contract is a cross-draw pairing whose legs are nearly independent and whose joint is the product of marginals with a small shared-conditions correction; cross-surface, carry-over and health-persistence inputs apply only to a same-player reading that is not listed. Misreading the structure gives an impossible or double-counted probability.
stages.distribution: Deterministic structural classification of the intersection; wrong classification gives errors that do not depend on any data.

stages.name: Marginal title probability for each leg
stages.description: Each leg needs its own title probability from a path simulation, with the field known only up to the entries and the draw. These marginals are the baseline; their errors propagate multiplicatively into the joint.
stages.distribution: Marginals between 0.5% and 40%; their product for two or three legs is small, so relative errors matter.

stages.name: Shared latent strength across surfaces
stages.description: Conditional (same-player multi-event reading; not used by the live KXATPWTA cross-draw pairing). A player's strengths on clay and grass are correlated but not identical. The conditional probability of the second title given the first depends on the covariance of his surface-specific ratings, so a hard-court rating gap is only partly informative about grass.
stages.distribution: Correlation between surface ratings of about 0.5-0.8; joint posterior over surfaces rather than independent estimates.

stages.name: Health and availability persistence
stages.description: The probability a player is fit for the second leg given he won the first depends on injury persistence and on the load of the first leg; a long run through seven rounds raises the risk of niggles but also signals current fitness. The shared health state couples all legs for that player.
stages.distribution: Positive persistence of fitness state across consecutive events; injury hazard rises after long runs and after heavy loads.

stages.name: Event-to-event load and calendar gap
stages.description: Conditional (same-player multi-event reading; not used by the live KXATPWTA cross-draw pairing). The days between legs and the minutes on court in the first leg set recovery, and the change of surface adds a transition cost. A short gap with a long first leg lowers the second leg's probability; a long gap reduces the link.
stages.distribution: Small mean shifts in match-win probability with threshold behaviour at short gaps; interaction with surface transition.

stages.name: Joint simulation, dependence among rivals and settlement collapse
stages.description: The joint probability is obtained by simulating the legs with the shared player state, including the dependence among players in the same bracket, and the combination collapses to the remaining legs as outcomes arrive. Dependence among rivals (a top player's absence helps the others) enters through the bracket correlation.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution with positive dependence along the same player and negative dependence among rivals in the same event; resolved legs convert to conditional probabilities.

coaching_scheme.note: No coaching or scheme variable is observable across tournament legs; coach changes act slowly and are absorbed into ratings and form, so there is no separate combination-level coaching quantity.

environment.note: Simultaneous men's and women's legs at one major share court pace, ball and weather; ten.venue_speed_history and ten.wind_indoor carry that weak common shock, with a verified per-event pace index still missing (cb_environment_gap).

game_context_script.note: No in-match script governs a combination of tournament titles; match-level script effects are inside the marginal path simulation and do not create a separate combination driver.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities beyond the fixed number of rounds in each leg; volume enters only as workload in minutes, which is handled under situational inputs.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion rates per point are embedded in the match probabilities of the marginal simulation; the combination contract has no extra conversion quantity of its own.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating and rule differences between legs (for example final-set formats) change marginals slightly but have no combination-specific mechanism.

ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.label: Cross-surface rating covariance
ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.mechanism: Joint posterior of a player's hard, clay and grass ratings, which determines how much a title on one surface predicts another.
ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.rationale: Treating each surface rating as independent makes consecutive-title joint probabilities too low; a pooled rating treats them as identical and makes them too high.
ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.measurement: Fit a hierarchical Elo model with a player-level vector (hard, clay, grass) and a covariance matrix Sigma estimated across players (typical correlation 0.5-0.8); report posterior covariance for each pair of surfaces for the player; use it in the joint simulation to draw correlated surface-specific strengths. As-of: before the first leg.
ten.cross_surface_rating_covariance.why: Not used by the live KXATPWTA series, whose rules name a man and a woman at one major (different players, separate draws); context only for an unlisted same-player combination. Provides the shared latent strength parameter that makes legs dependent.

ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.label: Event-to-event carryover after a title
ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.mechanism: Empirical probability of winning the next event given a title at the previous one, by calendar gap and surface change.
ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.rationale: The combination probability needs P(leg 2 | leg 1), which depends on the load of leg 1, the gap and the surface transition; the historical frequency of consecutive major titles provides a calibration target.
ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.measurement: From history of pairs of consecutive majors compute P(title at event 2 | title at event 1) for the same player by gap days (<=21, 22-42, >42) and surface change (clay to grass, grass to hard), as a ratio to the product of marginal probabilities; shrink the ratio toward the model-implied ratio with weight n/(n+8). As-of: before the first leg.
raw_data: major winners by year and event
ten.slam_to_slam_carryover.why: Not used by the live KXATPWTA series, whose rules name a man and a woman at one major (different players, separate draws); context only for an unlisted same-player combination. Supplies the empirical dependence that the model's joint simulation must reproduce.

ten.health_persistence_between_events.label: Health persistence between consecutive events
ten.health_persistence_between_events.mechanism: Probability a player is fit for event j+1 given fit at event j and a deep run, estimated from consecutive entries.
ten.health_persistence_between_events.rationale: Shared health links legs for one player; persistence differs by age and prior load.
ten.health_persistence_between_events.measurement: Unit = (player, consecutive scheduled events j, j+1 at which the player was on the entry list in j+1 and had played in j). y = 1 if the player played a match in j+1. Features: age bin (<25,25-30,30-34,35+), rounds won in j, total minutes in j, gap days; logistic with ridge (equiv. shrinkage n/(n+30)). Restrict to players ranked top 50 at the entry deadline of j+1; as-of = j+1 entry list publication. Withdrawals are identified from entry lists, not from absence of rows.
ten.health_persistence_between_events.why: Not used by the live KXATPWTA series, whose rules name a man and a woman at one major (different players, separate draws); context only for an unlisted same-player combination. Provides the persistence of the shared health state across legs.

ten.leg_resolution_state.label: Leg resolution state and conditional collapse
ten.leg_resolution_state.mechanism: State of each leg (open, won, lost) and the conditional probability of the remaining legs.
ten.leg_resolution_state.rationale: A combination whose first leg has resolved Yes is just the remaining legs' joint probability; a lost leg makes it zero; the leg structure determines how the conditional probability collapses as legs resolve.
ten.leg_resolution_state.measurement: Track per contract each leg status with timestamp; compute P(combo | resolved legs) from the joint simulation conditional on resolved legs; flag combinations whose legs have mutually exclusive outcomes; as-of: official result time.
ten.leg_resolution_state.why: Each KXATPWTA pairing's legs (men's and women's singles of one major) and their status: after one leg resolves the pairing equals the other leg's marginal or is dead, so unconditional joint probabilities must not be used once a leg has resolved.

ten.joint_event_correlation.reason: Defined only as an outcome of the contract, so it is the quantity being forecast rather than an input; its measurable drivers (cross-surface covariance, health persistence, bracket structure) carry the roles and it is used only as a calibration target.

ten.path_difficulty_sim.reason: Gives each leg's marginal and the bracket dependence; correct engine, but the joint must share the player state across legs.

ten.bracket_correlation.reason: Matters for mutually exclusive legs and rival dependence; output of the simulation rather than an input.

ten.pre_draw_field.reason: Entry lists define who can win each leg; snapshots needed, especially for later legs not yet entered.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Per-surface marginal strength; the missing piece is the covariance across surfaces.

ten.fitness.reason: Shared health state is the main driver of dependence across legs for a single player.

ten.workload_minutes.reason: Load between legs matters in tight calendars; effect is small and threshold-like.

m.rules_text.reason: The KXATPWTA rules define the legs (men's and women's singles of one named major) and make any withdrawal a No for the pairing; read per pairing.

m.external_lines.reason: Marginal sportsbook prices are benchmarks; using them as inputs would import the market's own correlation assumptions.

ten.form.reason: Recent form is in ratings; for combos its role is the carry-over effect, measured better by event-to-event data.

ten.motivation.reason: Event priority matters for non-majors in a combination across tour events; weak at majors.

interactions.mechanism: Two surface ratings of the same player are drawn from a correlated joint posterior; high covariance raises the probability of winning both and low covariance behaves like independence, so the joint probability depends on a second-moment parameter, not only on means.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the same marginals with covariance 0 and 0.7 and compare joint title probabilities with historical frequencies of consecutive major titles.

interactions.mechanism: The chance of arriving fit at the second leg is the persistence probability reduced by the load of the first; long runs lower fitness but also signal fit state, so the multiplicative load effect is small but measurable.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress start probability at the next event on prior minutes interacted with age.

interactions.mechanism: After a short gap (under three weeks) fatigue and surface transition cost reduce the next leg's chance; beyond about six weeks the carryover disappears, so the link has a threshold in the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin pairs of events by gap and compute the ratio of joint to product-of-marginals frequency.

interactions.mechanism: For the same-player reading, a high surface covariance raises the probability of a second title given the first mainly when the second leg's field is thin at the top (key rivals absent or injured); against a deep field the covariance matters less because the per-match upset risk dominates, so the covariance effect scales with field concentration.
interactions.how_to_test: Across past consecutive event pairs for one player, regress second-leg title on first-leg title interacted with a top-rival concentration measure of the second field; compare against the main effects alone.

interactions.mechanism: When a player is injured the combination probability falls to near zero for all his legs at once, while when healthy the legs are close to independent given ratings; the joint is a mixture over health regimes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the joint distribution of consecutive titles conditional on an injury flag at the first event.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic decline in cumulative first-leg minutes
nonlinearities.why: The chance of arriving fit at the second leg falls slowly with moderate load and faster beyond a heavy first-leg workload, so the joint probability of two titles is not linear in the first run's length.
Joint title probability increases convexly with the correlation of surface ratings because the intersection depends on the upper tail of a bivariate distribution.
Accumulated minutes reduce next-leg probability only after a long run with a short gap; below that threshold the effect is not distinguishable from zero.

contract.settlement_definition: Each market is a binary that one named player wins the named professional match by one specific set score, for example 'If Arthur Nagel wins the Jacob Fearnley vs Arthur Nagel ... match ... by a set score of 2-1, then the market resolves to Yes'. Yes requires both the winner and the loser's set tally to match, so the four best-of-three rungs (A 2-0, A 2-1, B 2-0, B 2-1) are mutually exclusive and sum to one for a completed match. Non-occurrence before the first ball resolves to a fair price, postponements stay open for up to two weeks, and the sampled retirement sentence says only that markets that can be unconditionally settled from play already completed settle on that play; the rest of the sentence is cut off in the sample. Games, tiebreak scores and margin inside sets are irrelevant. The source of truth is not named in the sampled text (presumably the governing league's recorded score).

rules_evidence.quote: by a set score of 2-1, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Yes needs the named winner and the exact set tally; the strike is winner-specific, not a total or spread.

rules_evidence.quote: If a retirement occurs, all markets that can be unconditionally settled
rules_evidence.establishes: On retirement, rungs that are already decided by completed sets settle and the remaining rungs are left to the rest of the clause (truncated in the sample).

rules_evidence.quote: If the match does not occur (signaled by a ball being played) due to a player injury, walkover, forfeiture, or any other cancellation (all before the match starts), the market will resolve to a fair price
rules_evidence.establishes: A match that never starts pays a fair price, so pre-start withdrawal is not a Yes/No loss.

variants_and_edge_cases: Best-of-three scores (2-0, 2-1) at WTA events and most ATP events versus best-of-five (3-0, 3-1, 3-2) at men's Slams; the rung set depends on the event format, which is not part of the strike text and must be read from the event.

Retirement mid-match: if player A has won set 1 and B retires, play already completed decides only B 2-0 (No at once); A 2-0, A 2-1 and B 2-1 were all still reachable, so none of them is unconditionally settled and the cut-off remainder of the retirement clause decides them (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS). At 1-1 a retirement settles both 2-0 rungs No and leaves both 2-1 rungs to the unseen clause.

Match tiebreak formats (10-point match tiebreak replacing a third set in doubles and some junior or exhibition events) make the 'set score' of 2-1 hinge on whether a tiebreak counts as a set; not stated in the rules sample.
Fair-price resolution applies only before the first ball, so a favourite who retires after one game leaves the 2-0 market in the 'can it be settled' branch rather than at a pre-start fair price.
contract.settlement_data_source: Governing league's recorded match score (set tally); the sampled rules do not name a specific data vendor or webpage.

mechanism.summary: The exact set score is the match winner combined with a count of how many sets the loser took, so it is a distribution over the paths of a short race rather than a single probability. Each set outcome depends on the pair's point-level serve and return strengths, on who serves first in that set, and on whether the set reaches a tiebreak. The sets are not independent: a latent day-level form shock and in-match physical state push the same player to win consecutive sets, which fattens 2-0 and 3-0 mass relative to independent sets, while a rallying underdog's stamina or an opponent's late-set fade pushes mass into deciders. The favourite's 2-0 frequency also depends on the quality of the tail, not just the mean, because 2-1 and 2-0 for the same player differ only in whether the underdog snatches one set, which is the tail event of the first set. The contract itself adds a truncation layer: a retirement can decide some rungs but not others, so the settlement rule decides which rungs carry retirement risk.

stages.name: Format and rung inventory
stages.description: Before probabilities exist, the format fixes which scorelines are possible: best-of-three gives four outcomes, best-of-five gives six, doubles with a match tiebreak give a different set structure. The deciding-set rule at 6-6 (tiebreak versus advantage) changes how long a deciding set can last but not the set tally, so format mostly acts by fixing the rung grid and the number of sets in which dependence can compound.
stages.distribution: Deterministic discrete support (4 or 6 outcomes) with the winner-specific split; no randomness at this stage but a wrong format coding is a total error.

stages.name: Set-one win probability for each player
stages.description: The first set is the cleanest read of the pair edge because no in-match history has accrued. The probability that A wins set 1 follows from A's and B's serve-point and return-point strengths and the chance that the set goes to a tiebreak. It is flatter than the match-win probability: a 75% match favourite may be only 62-65% to win the first set.
stages.distribution: Binomial-like around 0.5-0.7 for tour favourites; hold probabilities near 0.8 produce frequent 6-6 outcomes with a coin-flip-like tiebreak.

stages.name: First-server sequence and serve-order advantage
stages.description: Who serves first in each set is deterministic given the starting server and the parity of games in prior sets, and a tiebreak resets the order. Serving first matters more when hold rates are high: a big server who serves first is a few points more likely to win the set, and the advantage rotates across sets so that sets one and three share the same first server in an even-game match but not after a tiebreak.
stages.distribution: Discrete deterministic assignment with a small probability shift (roughly 1-5 points of set-win probability) that scales with the server's hold rate.

stages.name: Between-set dependence and state transitions
stages.description: The probability of winning set 2 depends on who won set 1. Part of this is latent: a player who plays well on the day plays well in both sets. Part is real in-match change: tactics adjustment by the loser, physical fade, momentum. The result is a 2x2 (or bo5 tree) of conditional set-win probabilities that cannot be reconstructed from the match-winner price alone.
stages.distribution: Positive correlation between set outcomes; the conditional probability for the favourite who loses set 1 usually stays above 50% but falls by several points; distribution is bimodal across player types.

stages.name: Length of match and decider incidence
stages.description: Whether the match reaches a deciding set depends on closeness of the pair and on expected length. Long sets, tiebreaks and slow courts raise the probability of 2-1 and 3-2 scorelines for either player while a very lopsided pair converts mass to 2-0 or 3-0. The expected number of service games sets the probability mass of tiebreaks in each set.
stages.distribution: Counts of sets with a heavy mass at the minimum; the decider probability is a smooth convex function of how even the pair is.

stages.name: Retirement truncation and which rungs it settles
stages.description: If a player retires, completed sets fix some rungs as No while others stay unsettled, and the rest of the retirement clause governs them. The share of mass carried by retirement is small but concentrated in the trailing or injured player's rung and in the early-set cases where the unconditional rule helps least.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event with timing: more likely just after set 1 or in the middle of set 2; asymmetric between the leader and the trailer.

role_personnel.note: Singles exact-score markets have no lineup or role variable; the participating players are fixed by the contract and any replacement voids the match to fair price before the first ball.

availability_news.note: Pre-match fitness and withdrawal signals shift mass between 2-0 and 2-1 for an impaired starter and raise the retirement share; retirement_timing_profile is only the historical outcome statistic of when retirements occur, kept as the conditional rung-settlement input.

coaching_scheme.note: Between-set coaching and tactical adjustment exist but have no observable pre-match proxy at set resolution; their aggregate effect is the between-set state transition measured in within_match_dependence.

environment.note: Court speed, ball and indoor/outdoor state set the hold level and tiebreak incidence, which move the 2-0/2-1 split; match_length_expectation is derived from hold and stays under pace_volume only.

ten.set_first_server_sequence.label: First server in each set (serve-order sequence)
ten.set_first_server_sequence.mechanism: Which player serves first in each set is a deterministic function of the start of the match and game parity, and first-serve shifts set-win probability.
ten.set_first_server_sequence.rationale: The existing catalog models hold and break but does not carry set-by-set serve order; for evenly matched big servers a coin-toss-driven first-serve advantage shifts the 2-0 versus 2-1 split. A tiebreak resets the rotation, so conditional on a tiebreak in set 1 the order in set 2 differs from the no-tiebreak case.
ten.set_first_server_sequence.measurement: Serve order after toss: set 1 first server S1 (from toss; unknown pre-match, treat as 0.5/0.5 until announced). Set k first server = opponent of the player who served the last game of set k-1 unless set k-1 ended with a tiebreak, in which case the player who received first in that tiebreak serves first. Compute P(set win | first server) by running the game-level chain for each of the 12-game sequences. Output per-set first-server probabilities conditional on tiebreak history. As-of: toss result (about 15 minutes before play) for the live case; pre-match treat unknown.
ten.set_first_server_sequence.why: Turns a flat set-win probability into the true sequence-specific one for each rung.

ten.straight_set_share_curve.label: Empirical straight-set share by pre-match edge
ten.straight_set_share_curve.mechanism: Probability that the winner takes the match without dropping a set as a function of pair edge, tour and format.
ten.straight_set_share_curve.rationale: This is a calibration curve (not a market price): it tells how much of the match-win probability mass historically converts to the sweep versus decider scorelines, which a purely i.i.d. model gets wrong.
ten.straight_set_share_curve.measurement: From Sackmann match scores for the past ten years, compute for bins of pre-match Elo-implied win probability (in 5-point bins, split by tour, best_of, surface) the share of matches won 2-0/3-0 and the share reaching a decider; shrink bin shares toward a logistic fit with weight n/(n+40); report P(2-0 | A wins) and P(deciding set). As-of: ratings available before each historical match.
ten.straight_set_share_curve.why: Provides the empirical anchor for the 2-0 versus 2-1 split that the existing catalog leaves to a latent parameter.

ten.retirement_timing_profile.label: Retirement timing distribution by set
ten.retirement_timing_profile.mechanism: When a retirement happens decides which exact-score rungs are already settled.
ten.retirement_timing_profile.rationale: A retirement after set 1 resolves different rungs than one in set 3; the existing retirement base rate does not carry timing.
ten.retirement_timing_profile.measurement: Parse every Sackmann score ending in RET/DEF: completed sets, games per player in the interrupted set, retiring player (the loser). Outputs by tour x best_of x round group, shrunk toward tour pooled with n/(n+30): P(retire before completing set 1/2/3), P(retiring player trailing), distribution of total games completed and of games margin D at stoppage (with P(D>1.5), P(count>k) for each strike k). Rows with missing interrupted-set score flagged and treated as censored for games counts. Data before as-of only.

ten.set_dist.reason: The joint set-score distribution is the object being priced, an output of the model rather than an independent input; its measurable ingredients are straight_set_share_curve, within_match_dependence, hold_break and format, so set_dist is retained only as the target representation.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Sets the pair edge from which set win probabilities are built; same role as in the winner market, adding nothing score-specific on its own.

ten.within_match_dependence.reason: The parameter that moves mass between 2-0 and 2-1; weakly identified, so it needs calibration from point-by-point data.

ten.hold_break.reason: Component for set win probabilities; not independently informative about the score split once set_dist is fit.

ten.decider_record.reason: Players' deciding-set records are tiny samples and mostly noise around fitness; better as first-set-winner conversion rate pooled across the tour.

ten.format.reason: Fixes the rung grid (best-of-three vs five) and match-tiebreak behaviour; a wrong format is a total error.

ten.fatigue.reason: Fatigue matters for later sets and deciders only; weak for 2-0 rungs.

ten.retirement_settlement_rules.reason: The retirement clause is truncated in the sample, so it decides which rungs settle; primary despite being a rules input.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Its catalog measurement fits a distribution to Kalshi mid prices across rungs and reports an implied PMF, so it is market-derived: useful only to benchmark and sanity-check model rung probabilities (monotonicity, sum-to-one), never as an outcome input or a coverage claim.

ten.serve_return.reason: Raw surface serve-point and return-point win rates are the unadjusted ingredient of the pair point model; they are a different quantity from an Elo-type rating, so not a duplicate of surface_rating, but they must enter only in opponent-adjusted form (ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return).

ten.tiebreak.reason: Tiebreak win rates regress heavily to serve strength; only matters in how many sets reach 6-6, covered by hold probability.

ten.match_length_expectation.reason: Expected service games per set determine tiebreak incidence; useful but derived from hold probabilities, so not a free variable. Verdict kept at KEEP_SECONDARY in all tennis records where it feeds a count or a tiebreak/decider rung (exact score, totals, aces).

interactions.mechanism: The correlation between sets scales with the size of the favourite's edge: for a large edge a shared form shock raises 2-0 mass more than for an even pair, because the shock moves a larger spread of the pair gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit set-2 win probability given set-1 result separately by Elo-gap bin and test whether the conditional uplift grows with the gap.

interactions.mechanism: Serving first adds an early game lead, and the lead is worth more when break chances are rare; for two big servers the first-server advantage in set win is larger than for return-dominant clay pairs.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress set outcome on first-server flag interacted with the pair's average hold probability in point-by-point data.

interactions.mechanism: Within a pre-match edge bin the straight-set share is not fixed: slower courts and weaker servers lengthen sets and push mass from 2-0 to 2-1 (and from 3-0/3-1 to 3-2), while a very lopsided pair stays near its edge-bin share whatever the pace. The pace effect therefore matters most for mid-edge pairs, giving a conditional rather than additive link.
interactions.how_to_test: Within each 5-point Elo-implied edge bin regress the indicator of a decider on expected service games per set (from hold rates) and its interaction with the edge-bin centre; compare out-of-sample log loss against the edge-only curve.

interactions.mechanism: In best-of-five the dependence between sets compounds across more transitions, so the same latent shock raises 3-0 and 3-2 mass differently than it does in best-of-three.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate bo3 and bo5 with the same shock variance and compare the scoreline distribution to historical Slam and tour frequencies.

interactions.mechanism: The rung affected by a retirement depends on when it happens: a retirement before set 2 settles no 2-1 rung while one in set 3 leaves 2-1 open; the regime is set by timing.
interactions.how_to_test: Enumerate historical retirements by completed sets and count which exact-score rungs would have been settled unconditionally.

nonlinearities.shape: concave in the 2-0 share given a win
nonlinearities.why: As the rating gap grows, P(2-0 | favourite wins) rises quickly at first then saturates near 1 because the underdog only needs one set to avoid it, and that saturation is flatter than in the match-win probability.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic-saturating in edge: P(2-0 | win) rises with the edge then flattens
nonlinearities.why: Straight-set share given a win rises with the pre-match edge but saturates near the tail because even heavy favourites drop a set through tiebreaks and day-form shocks; the shrunken binned curve (n/(n+40)) captures the flattening that an i.i.d. set chain overstates.
Decider incidence rises faster than linearly as expected games per set grow because each additional 6-6 set both lengthens the match and keeps it closer.

contract.settlement_definition: Six series are filed here: KXATPS1GWINNER, KXATPS2GWINNER, KXATPS3GWINNER, KXATPS4GWINNER (rules text recovered from archived markets), KXATPS5GWINNER and KXATPGWINNER (title only). Each market is a binary on one named player winning one numbered game of one numbered set: 'If Sho Shimabukuro wins game 10 in set 1 in the ... match ..., then the market resolves to Yes'. The set number is fixed by the series (S1..S5) and the game number by the market, so whether the named player is serving (a hold) or receiving (a break) follows from the first-server sequence and is not stated. If the match never starts (injury, walkover, forfeiture, cancellation before the first ball) the market resolves to a fair price; a postponed match stays open until the rescheduled match finishes (within two weeks). On retirement, 'all markets that can be unconditionally settled base[d on p...]' settle on completed play; the game-winner samples are cut off at 'based on p', so the rest of the clause is not visible. The text is silent on a named game that is never reached (set ends before game N, or set 4/5 not played), on whether game 13 (the tiebreak) counts as a game, and on the source of truth.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sho Shimabukuro wins game 10 in set 1 in the Sho Shimabukuro vs Stefanos Sakellaridis professional tennis match
rules_evidence.establishes: The object is one numbered game of one numbered set won by the named player; game number and set number are both part of the strike.

rules_evidence.quote: If Max Houkes wins game 6 in set 4 in the Martin Damm Jr vs Max Houkes professional tennis match
rules_evidence.establishes: Set-4 game markets exist, so the named game is conditional on the match reaching a fourth set (best-of-five or an unusual format) and on the set reaching game 6.

rules_evidence.quote: If the match does not occur (signaled by a ball being played) due to a player injury, walkover, forfeiture, or any other cancellation (all before the match starts), the market will resolve to a fair price
rules_evidence.establishes: A match that never starts settles at a fair price, not Yes/No.

rules_evidence.quote: If a retirement occurs, all markets that can be unconditionally settled
rules_evidence.establishes: After a retirement only markets already decided by completed play settle on it; the treatment of the remaining markets (including an unplayed named game) is in the cut-off part of the clause.

variants_and_edge_cases: Hold versus break: the named game's server is determined by who served first in the set (toss for set 1, game parity and tiebreak rule for later sets), so 'player X wins game 10' is a hold for one player and a break for the other; the rule text does not say which.
Unreached game: a set that ends 6-2 has eight games, so a game-10 market may never be played; the sampled rules do not say whether it resolves No, at a fair price or is cancelled (gw_no_rules).
Game 13 of a set is a tiebreak recorded as one game in the score; whether a tiebreak counts as 'game 13' for these markets is not stated.

Set existence: S3 markets need a third set and S4/S5 markets need four or five sets. All four sampled matches are best-of-three qualifying matches, yet KXATPS4GWINNER lists game 6 of set 4 in a 's-Hertogenbosch qualifier where a fourth set cannot exist; how such a structurally unreachable market settles is not stated (gw_no_rules), so set existence must be read from the event format, not assumed from the series.

Retirement: completed games settle; a retirement inside or before the named game falls into the cut-off part of the clause. Listing time (pregame versus during play) is not visible, so whether existence risk is priced in is unknown.
KXATPGWINNER and KXATPS5GWINNER are title only; they are assumed to share the S1-S4 wording.

mechanism.summary: A single tennis game is a race to four points with a two-point margin, and the server wins each point with a probability that is stable enough within a game to be treated as an independent trial. That makes the game outcome a closed-form function of one number, the server's current point-win probability against this returner, and of the point score at the time of trading. The hold probability is steeply nonlinear in that number: it moves from about 0.74 at 0.60 to 0.90 at 0.70. The real mechanism sits one level up: the probability is not the pregame average but a running posterior that is updated by each point already played in the match, shifted by ball age, first-serve percentage drift, wind, an emerging injury, and the pressure of the score. Because the market is traded while play continues, a second layer matters: the score feed that Kalshi settles on and the feed that traders see are not the same clock. The recovered rules add an existence layer: each contract names game N of set M before that game is necessarily reached, so the traded probability is P(set M is played and reaches game N) times P(named player wins that game | reached), and the identity of the server in game N follows deterministically from the first-server sequence and the score path.

stages.name: Pregame serve-point prior for the server in this pair
stages.description: Before any point is played the model needs a prior spw for the server against this returner on this court. It comes from each player's serve quality, the returner's return quality and the court pace, with an uncertainty that is large enough that a one-point error in spw changes the hold chance by about three points at the margin where deuce games are decided.
stages.distribution: Beta-like distribution around 0.58-0.72 on tour; the prior has an effective sample size of a few hundred points rather than a point estimate.

stages.name: In-match posterior update of spw
stages.description: Every point already played in the match updates the server's spw. A beta-binomial update with a prior strength of roughly 40-80 points, adjusted for the first-serve in-percentage drift observed so far, gives a running estimate that departs from the pregame prior when a player is serving unusually well or badly, with the update giving less weight to a few points than to a full set.
stages.distribution: Posterior of a binomial rate: variance shrinks like 1/n of points played; the prior weight, not the data, dominates in the first few games.

stages.name: Game state transition at point level
stages.description: The game is a Markov chain on the point score: 0-0, 15-0, ... deuce, advantage. The win probability at each score is a deterministic function of spw; at 30-30 or deuce the leverage is highest and a probability error costs the most. Break points are pressure points where small differences in the server's first-serve rate matter more than their average.
stages.distribution: Absorbing chain with an infinite-tail deuce loop; discrete scores with sharply non-uniform leverage.

stages.name: Court, ball and weather modifiers during play
stages.description: Wind direction switches at changeovers, at many events new balls are introduced after the first seven games and then every nine (the schedule differs by event and is unverified here), and the sun or roof state can change during the match. These modify spw in a game-specific way that is partially knowable from the order of serving, and which the pregame prior ignores.
stages.distribution: Small systematic shifts of roughly 1-3 points of spw with game-parity structure rather than random noise.

stages.name: Physical deterioration and in-match health
stages.description: Medical timeouts, visible movement problems, drops in first-serve speed and increased double faults are signs the server's spw will fall during the match. The signal arrives through the live feed and television rather than any pre-match source and is binary-like in its effect: a trained trainer visit lowers the hold probability by several points for the rest of the match.
stages.distribution: Regime change with a small probability but a large shift in the serve rate; positively skewed risk of a worse spw.

stages.name: Settlement rule and interrupted-game handling
stages.description: The market resolves on the official result of the named game. The recovered text settles a match that never starts at a fair price, keeps a postponed match open up to two weeks, and on retirement settles only markets that can be unconditionally settled from play already completed (the game-winner samples are cut off at 'based on p'); the remainder of that clause is not visible, so a retirement before or inside the named game, a named game that is never reached, a game decided by point or code penalty and a tiebreak counted as game 13 remain unread. Feed timing is excluded from this stage on purpose: it affects when a trader can act, not who wins the game.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete regime: P(interruption) per game is very small and concentrated at high-leverage scores; otherwise the outcome is the Bernoulli chain of stage s3.

stages.name: Existence of the named game and identity of its server
stages.description: The rules name game N of set M (S1-S5 series) for one player. Before that game starts the contract carries two extra uncertainties: whether the match reaches set M (a set-3 market needs 1-1 in best-of-three, set 4/5 markets need best-of-five) and whether set M lasts N games (game 10 needs both players to have at least four games, so a 6-3 set never reaches it; game 13 exists only at 6-6). Given existence, game N is served by the player who served first in set M if N is odd, otherwise by the other, so the event is a hold for one player and a break for the other; the first server of set M depends on the toss and on the parity of games in previous sets.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli existence mass from the games-per-set and set-count distributions (discrete, heavily dependent on the hold gap) times a hold or break probability; parity creates a two-point mixture before the server of set M is known.

role_personnel.note: A game is played by two fixed singles players with no lineup or substitution; roles are limited to who serves, covered by server_game_state, not a personnel question.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching during a game is limited by rule and there is no observable tactical variable at game-resolution scale; any strategic shift appears in the point-win statistics.

pace_volume.note: Within a game there is no volume driver, but the contract's existence depends on how many games set M lasts and whether set M is played (stage s7), which these distributions supply.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and schedule effects enter through the pre-match spw prior and are far smaller than in-match information; no separate game-level schedule variable is identifiable.

settlement_contract.note: Rules text exists for the S1-S4 series (fair price before the first ball, two-week postponement, retirement settles only unconditionally decided markets); the unreached-game, tiebreak-as-game-13 and cut-off retirement remainder stay open (gw_no_rules); KXATPGWINNER/KXATPS5GWINNER are title only.

ten.in_match_spw_posterior.label: In-match running serve-point posterior
ten.in_match_spw_posterior.mechanism: The server's spw during the match is a posterior combining the pregame pair prior with the points played so far.
ten.in_match_spw_posterior.rationale: The existing catalog lists the live point stream but not the update rule; the trade-off between prior weight and observed points is the central modelling choice.
ten.in_match_spw_posterior.measurement: Beta-binomial: spw_post = (k*spw_prior + wins_so_far)/(k + points_served_so_far) with k fit by maximising held-out game log-likelihood on historical point sequences (start with k=60 points, range 30-120); allow a separate k for first-serve points and second-serve points; add an exponential forgetting factor of 0.98 per point when a medical signal fires. Updated after every point, timestamped to the feed clock.
free_sources: Sackmann slam point-by-point for calibration of k
raw_data: point sequences with server and winner
ten.in_match_spw_posterior.why: Directly determines the game win probability at each score and is where pregame information is handed off to live information.

ten.ball_change_cycle.label: Ball age and ball-change schedule
ten.ball_change_cycle.mechanism: New balls favour the server and change the ratio of hold probability across the first games after a ball change.
ten.ball_change_cycle.rationale: Slam and tour rules change balls after seven games and then every nine games; a game right after a ball change is played with livelier balls. The magnitude is small and event-specific, so the sign and size must be estimated, not assumed.
ten.ball_change_cycle.measurement: Register per event-year: first_change_after = a (e.g. 7 or 9), interval = b (9 or 11), warmup_counts flag. Games played before game g = g-1; new balls are used in game g iff g-1 >= a and (g-1-a) mod b == 0; fresh = that indicator. Estimate delta_hold = coefficient on fresh in logit(hold) ~ server + returner + surface + event + fresh from Slam point-by-point (game level), report as change in hold probability (pp), shrunk to 0 with n/(n+500) games. Event not in register -> missing, not imputed.
ten.ball_change_cycle.why: Provides a deterministic game-level modifier with known timing, unlike the unobservable form shocks.

ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.label: Deuce-court versus ad-court serve and return asymmetry
ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.mechanism: A player's serve and return win rates differ between the deuce and ad sides, and break points are mostly played on the ad side in this lead-in.
ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.rationale: The point score determines which side the point is played from, so game state and side are tied; lefties and right-handers differ systematically.
ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.measurement: From charted points, estimate spw_deuce and spw_ad per server and the returner's rpw on each side with shrinkage n/(n+80); expected game win probability computed with side-specific spw along the score path (e.g. 30-40 and 40-40 on the ad side). Sparse for non-charted matches.
ten.court_side_point_asymmetry.why: Matters because the highest-leverage points of a game (deuce, ad-in, break point) are played mostly on one side.

ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.label: Shot-clock and violation state
ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.mechanism: The serve clock and warnings change second-serve timing and can produce a lost first serve or point penalty inside a game.
ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.rationale: Time violations take away a first serve or award a point in limited cases; in tight finals the umpire's discretion varies and affects the point score directly.
ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.measurement: Count of time violations and code violations per match from official or broadcast logs; estimate violation hazard per player and chair umpire (shrunk n/(n+20)); for a live game include a binary flag if a warning has been issued. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for structured violation logs.
free_sources: Broadcast and official match reports (manual coding)
ten.shot_clock_and_violation_state.why: Provides the officiating channel for game-level outcomes that other inputs ignore.

ten.server_game_state.reason: The point score and server determine the game win probability given spw; essential and deterministic, not a predictor of spw.

ten.in_play.reason: Point-level state is the same information as the game state plus set score; keep one id for the score path and add posterior spw as the dynamic variable.

ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return.reason: The pregame prior for spw; still correct, but needs an explicit prior strength so the in-match update has weights.

ten.first_serve_in_variance.reason: Within-match first-serve percentage drift moves spw; at game scale it acts through the posterior, so keep as a state variable.

ten.break_point_luck.reason: Break-point conversion regression is a season-scale trait measured over hundreds of points; its effect on a single game is negligible and double counts with spw.

ten.score_feed_latency.reason: Latency of the settlement and public score feeds changes when a trader can act, not the probability the player wins the game; it is execution evidence kept outside the outcome chain, no longer a stage or interaction input and not primary.

ten.in_match_medical_signals.reason: Rare but high-impact regime change; hard to timestamp from structured data, so definition quality matters.

ten.wind_indoor.reason: Wind shifts spw by a point or two and flips at changeovers; indoor flag is trivial; limited by weather data granularity.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade tape is market data; it measures the price response and is not a determinant of the game outcome, so it belongs to execution analysis.

ten.serve_return.reason: Unadjusted surface rates are the raw ingredient of the adjusted prior; keeping both double counts.

ten.break_points.reason: Break points created/saved are outcomes of spw and rpw rather than independent drivers; only useful inside the live state, which ten.server_game_state already carries.

interactions.mechanism: Game win probability is a steep function of spw at deuce and break-point scores, so a given posterior error costs more at 30-30 than at 40-0; the value of better spw information is concentrated in the tight scores.
interactions.how_to_test: Evaluate log loss of the game outcome by score state under alternative prior weights k and compare the benefit by state.

interactions.mechanism: Ball freshness boosts big servers more than baseliners, so the new-ball uplift in hold probability is a multiple of the server's pace advantage and absent for weak servers.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact the new-ball flag with server ace rate in a hold regression on point-by-point games.

interactions.mechanism: Wind on one end lowers first-serve in-percentage there and makes second serves the key point; the effect appears only in games served into the wind and flips at changeovers.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress first-serve in% on wind component relative to the server's end per game parity.

interactions.mechanism: A medical timeout makes past points less representative of future serving, so the posterior should forget faster than the base update rule; ignoring the break underprices the receiver's break chance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare game outcomes after a trainer visit with predictions from slow-forgetting versus fast-forgetting posterior variants.

interactions.mechanism: If a game is cut short by retirement or suspension, the traded event settles differently depending on the point score reached: at 40-0 a rule that credits unconditionally decidable results behaves unlike a rule that voids an incomplete game. The settlement regime therefore switches the effective probability by score state, and matters most at the high-leverage deuce and break-point scores.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate historical interrupted games by point score at interruption and apply each candidate settlement rule to compute the traded-event probability; compare the spread between rules by score state.

nonlinearities.why: The closed-form game win probability moves from about 0.74 at spw 0.60 to 0.90 at 0.70, so equal posterior errors cost more in the 0.60-0.68 band than outside it.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise function of the point score
nonlinearities.why: Leverage differs by score: at 40-0 the server's hold probability is near 0.99 and nearly flat in spw, whereas at deuce it is almost the full S-curve.
When first-serve percentage drops below roughly 50% the server is forced onto second serves, and spw falls faster than linearly in the first-serve rate.

contract.settlement_definition: Two contract objects share this archetype. (1) Single-match winner (KXATPMATCH, KXWTAMATCH, KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH, KXWTACHALLENGERMATCH, KXATPDOUBLES, KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES, KXTENNISEXHIBITION with rules; KXATPGAME, KXWTAGAME title only): 'If Casper Ruud wins the Casper Ruud vs Carlos Alcaraz professional tennis match ... after a ball has been played, then the market resolves to Yes'. A match that never starts resolves to a fair price and a postponed match stays open up to two weeks; the sampled text has no retirement sentence before the disclaimer, so the opponent of a retiring player winning is tour convention, not text. (2) Named-round winner (KXATPAMT, KXATPMC, KXATPMIA, KXATPMAD, KXWTAIWO, KXWTAMIA, KXWTAMAD, KXWTADDF, all recovered from archived 2025 markets): 'If Jack Draper is a 2025 winner of the final of ATP Madrid, then the market resolves to Yes', with semifinal variants. These carry no secondary text, so walkover, retirement and non-occurrence treatment is unstated, and if listed before the pairing is set the event includes reaching the round. No overtime concept exists; source of truth is not named.

variants_and_edge_cases: Retirement after the first ball: the sampled winner rules say nothing about it (the retirement sentence appears only in the set/game/totals variants and is cut off in the sample), so the settlement of a retiring-favourite match is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Doubles series (KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPDOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES) settle a pair; doubles use no-ad scoring and a 10-point match tiebreak in place of a third set, which compresses the match and raises the variance of the winner outcome per point of edge.
Lower-level matches (Challenger) have thinner data, sometimes no live scoring feed, so the 'after a ball has been played' trigger and the settlement source can lag the real result.

Scope: these inputs are pre-match only. KXATPMATCH/KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH trade during play (sampled markets show both active and finalized status), but in-match state (score, server, medical timeout, live retirement hazard) is not an input here; it belongs to game_winner_inplay-type state inputs and no live-state input list exists for match-winner markets.

Series set after the reconciliation: eighteen series. Ten single-match series (eight with rules: KXATPMATCH, KXWTAMATCH, KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH, KXWTACHALLENGERMATCH, KXATPDOUBLES, KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES, KXTENNISEXHIBITION; KXATPGAME/KXWTAGAME title only) and eight tournament-named round-winner series with rules (KXATPAMT, KXATPMC, KXATPMIA, KXATPMAD, KXWTAIWO, KXWTAMIA, KXWTAMAD, KXWTADDF).

Named-round winner series ('a 2025 winner of the final/semifinal of X'): mechanically identical to the KXATPIWO/KXATPIT/KXATPMCO round-winner series filed under tournament_winner_futures; if listed before the round's pairing is known, Yes needs reaching and winning the round, and a walkover win in the named round or a withdrawal before it is unaddressed by any text.

mechanism.summary: A tennis match winner is the end of a nested counting process. Each service point is won by the server with probability that depends on that specific server-returner pair on that court: the server's serve quality, the returner's return quality, the court speed and ball, and the player's physical state on the day. Points aggregate into games through a deuce-amplifying hold function, games into sets through six-all tiebreak rules, and sets into the match through the best-of-three or best-of-five target, so a small point-level edge becomes a large winner edge. Day-level form shocks shared across points create overdispersion that lowers the favourite's edge relative to an i.i.d. chain. Before any of that happens a participation gate decides whether the contract has a match at all, and after play starts a retirement hazard can truncate the match before the count completes. The winner market is also the most liquid one, which makes it the anchor the other tennis archetypes are priced against.

stages.name: Participation and start gate
stages.description: Before the point model matters, a match must be played. Withdrawals after the draw, walkovers, late lucky-loser swaps and rain postponements decide whether the contract resolves at a fair price or runs to a result. The gate is almost entirely a function of news timing, order-of-play publication and entry-list status, and it is correlated with the injury state that also lowers a player's point-win rate if he does start.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per player with a hazard that spikes in the 24 hours before order of play; strongly clustered by player-injury state and tournament round.

stages.name: Latent strength on this specific court
stages.description: Each player has a latent ability on the match's court that is neither overall Elo nor raw surface Elo: it is a continuous function of court speed and ball behaviour. A big server's latent strength rises with court speed while a counter-puncher's falls, so two players with equal clay Elo are not equal at a fast indoor hard event. The estimate must also carry honest uncertainty for returners, juniors and players who recently moved between Challenger and tour level. For the three doubles series (KXATPDOUBLES, KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES) the unit of strength is the pair, not either player: ten.doubles_pair_strength (doubles ratings, partnership continuity) replaces the singles rating, and for KXTENNISEXHIBITION the rating gap is shrunk for format and effort (ten.exhibition_format_effort) because exhibition results carry little competitive signal.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like latent ability with heteroscedastic uncertainty; uncertainty is heavy-tailed for players with fewer than about 30 recent tour matches or after a layoff.

stages.name: Pair-specific serve and return point model
stages.description: Match probability is generated by two numbers: A's probability of winning a point on his serve against B's return and B's on his serve against A's return. They come from each player's serve quality and return quality relative to the tour average on this surface, plus pair interactions such as a big lefty slice serve into a weak ad-court backhand return. The pair of serve-point probabilities, not the gap in overall rating, drives games, sets and the match.
stages.distribution: Two correlated binomial rates; the two spw values are individually well estimated (0.60-0.70 on tour) but their difference is small, so estimation error of 1-2 points of spw already swings match probability by several percent.

stages.name: Day-of physical and scheduling modifiers
stages.description: Fatigue from the previous rounds, short turnaround, time-zone shift and in-tournament medical history move the two point-win probabilities down by small amounts on the day. These are modifiers to the s3 rates, not additional strength measures, and most of them are only observable as match minutes, rest days and public injury reports.
stages.distribution: Small mean shifts (about 0.5-2 points of spw) with a fat left tail for visibly injured players; correlated across rounds within a tournament.

stages.name: Points to games to sets to match with shared day shocks
stages.description: The two spw values are pushed through the game-hold function, set tiebreak rules and the sets-to-win target. A latent match-level form shock shared across points makes set outcomes positively correlated, which flattens the favourite's edge versus an i.i.d. chain, while best-of-five gives the stronger player more points to express the edge and doubles formats with match tiebreaks do the opposite.
stages.distribution: Discrete nested counts: games are geometric-like around deuce, sets are bounded random walks, match is a first-to-n race; overdispersion from the shared shock raises 2-1 and 3-2 frequency.

stages.name: Mid-match termination and settlement
stages.description: Retirements truncate the count: the player who is injured or physically spent stops, and the tour record gives the match to his opponent. This converts a stage-5 loss into a settled loss or an ambiguous outcome depending on wording. The hazard is higher in best-of-five, in heat, and for players who began the match visibly impaired, and it is the only stage where the winning side is chosen by an event unrelated to point-win rate.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event (roughly 1-3% of tour matches) concentrated in the trailing, injured player; tail risk is far larger for a favourite carrying a known injury.

stages.name: Named-round winner: reaching the round and winning it
stages.description: The eight tournament-named series (ATP Acapulco, Monte Carlo, Miami, Madrid; WTA Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, Dubai) settle on the named player being 'a winner of the semifinal/final'. Once the pairing is fixed this is the s3-s6 match model for that round. If the market is listed earlier, the probability is P(reach the named round) times P(win it | opponent distribution), computed by draw simulation over the remaining bracket with seed-dependent opponents, accumulated fatigue and per-round walkover hazard, so the named player's draw quarter matters as much as their rating.
stages.distribution: Product of per-round Bernoulli survivals along a draw path, mixed over the opponent distribution in each round; strongly right-skewed across players (most mass on top seeds) with negative dependence between players in the same section.

coaching_scheme.note: Tennis has no in-match substitution, rotation or play-calling decision that a pre-match variable can observe; coaching-staff changes act slowly through the rating and are indistinguishable from form at the single-match horizon.

pace_volume.note: A winner market is not a count: serve-point volume enters only through the best-of-three/five and match-tiebreak format, which is already carried by ten.format and the points-to-match transformation in ten.hold_break (a model component, not an extra measurable). No separate pace or volume input would change P(win).

officiating_rules.note: The official only affects the winner through line-call overrules and code violations, whose effect on a single match winner is below estimation noise; rules differences (final-set format, no-ad) are carried by ten.format instead.

ten.player_speed_slope.label: Player-specific court-speed response slope
ten.player_speed_slope.mechanism: A player's strength is a function of continuous court pace, not just a hard/clay/grass label.
ten.player_speed_slope.rationale: Overall Elo blends surfaces and surface Elo is a three-way categorical split. Court speed varies a lot inside 'hard' (Indian Wells slow, Paris indoor fast). Players differ in their sensitivity: big servers gain on fast courts, baseliners lose.
ten.player_speed_slope.measurement: For each player fit Elo_i(c)=Elo_i0 + beta_i*(CPI_c - mean CPI) with CPI from event ace-rate/hold-rate index over the previous three editions (hold% over tour average, with time-decay half-life one year). Estimate beta_i by ridge regression on that player's last ~120 tour matches using only matches completed before the as-of date; prior beta mean from serve profile (ace rate, height) with ridge penalty lambda ~ 20 matches. Output the speed-adjusted Elo for the match event. Leave-player-out rule: the event CPI used for player i is recomputed excluding every match involving player i (and the same player's other events), so beta_i is not fit against an index containing its own serve and return results; each remaining match's hold and ace residual is first adjusted for the two players' own tour-surface baselines to reduce field-composition contamination (field composition is still not fully removable, see mw_speed_index_source).

ten.player_speed_slope.why: Swaps a three-way categorical surface label for a continuous pace response so the winner price separates specialists at fast vs slow hard courts.

ten.level_transfer_offset.label: Challenger/ITF to tour rating offset
ten.level_transfer_offset.mechanism: Players move between Challenger/ITF and tour level, and ratings fitted on different pools are not on the same scale.
ten.level_transfer_offset.rationale: Kalshi lists Challenger matches (KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH, KXWTACHALLENGERMATCH) where one player may have 80% of recent matches at ITF level and the other on tour; a pooled Elo with a single scale overstates the lower-level player.
ten.level_transfer_offset.measurement: Pool all levels (tour, Challenger, ITF) in one Elo run. For each level L define offset_L = mean over players with >=5 matches at both L and tour level within the previous 24 months of (mean Elo after last 5 tour matches - mean Elo before first 5 matches...) i.e. the rating change across the crossing, shrunk by n_players/(n_players+25) toward 0, recomputed weekly from data before as-of. Rating used for a match = Elo + offset_L(player's pool). Use only crossings completed before as-of.

ten.doubles_pair_strength.label: Doubles pair strength and partnership continuity
ten.doubles_pair_strength.mechanism: A doubles winner is a pair-level outcome: net play, serve-plus-one patterns and chemistry matter beyond two individual singles ratings.
ten.doubles_pair_strength.rationale: KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPDOUBLES and KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES settle pairs that often formed days earlier. Singles rating is a weak proxy: doubles specialists with weak singles records dominate.
ten.doubles_pair_strength.measurement: Doubles Elo per player: start 1500, K=32 for first 30 doubles matches then 16, updated using the pair mean; shrunk d_i = 1500 + (elo_i-1500)*n_i/(n_i+15). Pair rating = 1500 + 0.6*mean(d_A-1500,d_B-1500) + 0.25*pair_elo_dev (0 if <5 shared matches) + 0.15*0.3*mean(singles_elo-1500) - debut_penalty, debut_penalty=20*max(0,1-prior_matches/10). Only matches before as-of; weights are placeholders to be fit by log loss.
raw_data: doubles match rows with 4 player ids, score, round
ten.doubles_pair_strength.why: Winner contracts on doubles pairs cannot be priced from singles ratings; the dedicated series are listed and their pairs change week to week.

ten.exhibition_format_effort.label: Exhibition format and effort proxy
ten.exhibition_format_effort.mechanism: Exhibitions use shortened formats and non-binding stakes, so the usual ability-to-result mapping is distorted.
ten.exhibition_format_effort.rationale: KXTENNISEXHIBITION is a winner market whose format may be short sets, a match tiebreak or time limit; player effort is discretionary and favourites may coast.
ten.exhibition_format_effort.measurement: Binary flags for event class (exhibition, invitational, team exhibition) plus format descriptors (sets to win, games per set, match-tiebreak, no-ad) coded from the event announcement; shrink the Elo-implied win probability toward 50% by a factor estimated from historical exhibition results (target shrink 0.6-0.8, to be fit when data exist). As-of: announcement date.
ten.exhibition_format_effort.why: Prevents applying tour-match calibration to exhibitions where effort and format differ from tour rules.

ten.walkover_slot_hazard.label: Walkover and late-withdrawal hazard by slot
ten.walkover_slot_hazard.mechanism: Pre-start walkovers and lucky-loser swaps remove a match from the payoff set or change the participants.
ten.walkover_slot_hazard.rationale: The sampled rule sends non-occurrence to a fair price, so the exposure is to price drift in the final hours before a withdrawal becomes public, not to a final loss. Hazard varies by round, event tier and days since last match.
ten.walkover_slot_hazard.measurement: Empirical day-level hazard h(round, tier, days_since_last_match, last_match_minutes>150, age>=33) = share of scheduled matches ending in a W/O score (withdrawal after the draw is made, including lucky-loser replaced slots) in the Sackmann-style score field; logistic regression with shrinkage toward round-level means (n/(n+30)). Sackmann score strings carry NO withdrawal timestamp, so this historical estimate is a single per-match rate; horizon-specific P(WO) at T-48h/T-12h/T-2h must be built from own-captured order-of-play and entry-list snapshots going forward (see unresolved mw_wo_vintage) and is not backfillable. As-of timestamp: order-of-play publication time.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Right base quantity; the categorical surface blend still hides within-surface court speed, covered by the new player_speed_slope, and needs honest handling of Challenger scale.

ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return.reason: Drives spw for the pair; must be the opponent-adjusted deviation form, not raw averages, and overlaps ten.serve_return as the raw ingredient.

ten.hold_break.reason: A transformation (spw to hold to match) rather than data; useful as a model component, not a separately measurable input for the winner market.

ten.format.reason: Best-of-three versus five (Slams for men) and doubles match tiebreaks change the edge amplification; cheap and exact to code.

ten.fitness.reason: Largest single-match shift when public; role fine, but timestamp vintage of the injury report matters more than the content.

ten.fatigue.reason: Effect is real late in events but small; define as minutes and sets in the last 7 days rather than a vague composite.

ten.court_cond.reason: Bundles altitude, ball, indoor and weather into one id; the speed component should be measured continuously, see player_speed_slope.

ten.h2h_style.reason: Head-to-head records average under 6 matches and mostly proxy ratings; keep only handedness/style flags, not raw win-loss counts.

ten.rating_uncertainty.reason: Matters for returners and Challenger names; operates as shrinkage on the gap rather than a level effect.

ten.retirement_settlement_rules.reason: Sampled winner text is silent on retirement, so this must be treated as an open contract question, not as a solved input.

ten.market_odds.reason: Bookmaker closing line is a price; per the brief a benchmark, not an input to evaluating the contract.

ten.market_margin_bias.reason: De-vig method concerns reading a market price, not the match mechanism; benchmark handling only.

ten.serve_return.reason: Raw surface spw/rpw are the unadjusted ingredient of the adjusted components; keep one definition to avoid double counting.

ten.form.reason: Recent results are already in Elo updates; as a separate input it double counts unless defined as residual vs rating with decay.

ten.second_serve_vulnerability.reason: Specific pair channel: break chances concentrate on second-serve points; informative only after serve/return rates are controlled.

ten.surface_similarity.reason: Pooling weights are a modelling device that stabilises thin grass samples rather than a measurable input.

ten.handedness.reason: Small effect (tenths of a point of spw) that is mostly reflected in lefties' own serve numbers; keep as a matchup flag.

ten.travel_timezone.reason: Largest effect in first-round matches after intercontinental swings; negligible by quarter-finals.

ten.suspension_postponement_risk.reason: Postponement keeps the market open for two weeks, so it changes timing and rest more than settlement; matters for fatigue carryover.

interactions.mechanism: A big server's rating gain from court pace multiplies with the event's measured pace index; on a fast indoor court the same server gains several Elo points while a counter-puncher loses them, which the surface label alone cannot represent.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress match outcome on Elo gap plus (beta_i - beta_j)*CPI_event and test the coefficient on the product against a model with surface dummies.

interactions.mechanism: Best-of-five amplifies the favourite's edge, but a shared day-level form shock reduces that amplification; the net direction flips when the shock variance is large relative to the per-point edge.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare calibration of winner probabilities for bo3 vs bo5 among equal-Elo-gap pairs with and without a latent form shock in the simulation.

interactions.mechanism: If a player starts injured, point-win rate falls and retirement probability rises; how the contract treats retirement decides whether that shifts the fair price in the same or opposite direction to the on-court outcome.
interactions.how_to_test: Split matches with an injury flag by whether the injured player was the favourite and measure how often the opponent is recorded the winner via RET.

interactions.mechanism: Fatigue effects emerge only after long previous matches (about 3 hours or five sets) and are larger in best-of-five, so the response is near zero below a load threshold then steepens.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin prior-match minutes and compare Elo-residuals by bin separately for bo3 and bo5.

interactions.mechanism: A player recently promoted from ITF to Challenger carries both a scale offset and a wide rating error, and the two compound: the winner price should shrink toward 50% more for the cross-level pair than for two same-level players.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare log loss of cross-level vs same-level Challenger matches under the offset-adjusted and unadjusted ratings.

nonlinearities.why: Hold probability is a steep logistic-like function of serve-point probability around 0.6-0.7, so a one-point spw error changes hold by roughly three points and match probability by more.

nonlinearities.shape: shrinkage toward 0.5 that decreases with sample size
nonlinearities.why: The winner probability for a heavy favourite is flattened more when its rating error is large; the shrink factor is roughly proportional to rating variance divided by variance plus pair noise.
Rest and minutes show little effect below a heavy-load cutoff (long match plus short turnaround) and a roughly linear penalty beyond it.

contract.settlement_definition: Three live series are filed here after the reconciliation and all carry rules text. KXATPNATWINNER: 'If an American woman wins the women's singles title in the 2026 US Open tennis tournament, then the market resolves to Yes', with nationalities 'designated by the Governing League' - a union over every compatriot in the named draw. KXATPNATSTAGE ('If 1+ Americans reach the Final in the 2026 US Open Men's Singles', greater_or_equal, floor 1) and KXWTANATSTAGE ('If 3+ Americans reach the Semifinals in the 2026 US Open Women's Singles', floor 3) are counts of compatriots reaching a named round with an N+ threshold; the Final holds at most two players and the semifinals four. None of the sampled texts states how a compatriot who reaches the round and then withdraws, a walkover into the round, or a change of designation is treated, and no source of truth is named. Team-competition contracts (Davis Cup, BJK Cup, United Cup, Laver Cup) are not listed and their rules are unknown. This record owns the union/count aggregation, collision structure and designation rules; tournament_winner_futures supplies the per-player path marginals.
