rules_evidence.quote: If 1+ Americans reach the Final in the 2026 US Open Men's Singles, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Stage-count contract with floor_strike 1 and strike_type greater_or_equal: count of compatriots reaching the named round, at most two for a Final.

rules_evidence.quote: If 3+ Americans reach the Semifinals in the 2026 US Open Women's Singles, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Thresholds above one exist (3+ of the four semifinal slots), so the full count distribution and quarter-final compatriot collisions are needed, not only the union.

variants_and_edge_cases: Nationality designation: KXATPNATWINNER and KXWTANATSTAGE defer to the governing league's designated nationality, so players competing under a neutral designation, with dual nationality or after a switch of allegiance are settlement edge cases not resolved by any text visible here. KXATPNATSTAGE's sampled text has no designation sentence at all.

Union versus count: 'an American wins' is a union over all compatriots in the draw (probability at least one), whereas '2+ Americans reach the Final' is a count with a threshold, and the two have different dependence structure (the Final can hold at most two players).

Walkover and withdrawal: the 'qualify but do not end up competing, still Yes' sentence belongs to KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE (tournament_winner_futures), not to the NATSTAGE texts, which only say 'reach the Final/Semifinals'; whether a compatriot who reaches the round and then withdraws, or advances into it by walkover, counts is not stated for any series here, and the title contract has no withdrawal sentence either.

Team events: tie-level results (best of three rubbers, with doubles as the decider), group-stage tie-break order, and a team withdrawing or forfeiting all create edge cases that the nationality-winner text does not cover.

Rules-text status: KXATPNATWINNER, KXATPNATSTAGE and KXWTANATSTAGE are now filed here and their rules are quoted; the count thresholds vary by series (1+ to the Final, 3+ to the Semifinals) so the archetype needs the whole count distribution. Verification is partial because withdrawal-after-reaching-the-round, designation source and source of truth are not stated.
contract.settlement_data_source: Governing league's designated nationality for each player and the official tournament or tie results; no vendor named.

mechanism.summary: A nationality contract asks whether any member of a national group achieves an individual outcome, so it is a union over the compatriots in a draw rather than a property of one player. The union is built from each player's individual path probability but is reduced by a structural dependence: two compatriots in the same half of a bracket cannot both reach the final, and every meeting between them removes one candidate with certainty. A count contract adds a threshold on the number of successes, which depends on the number of compatriots, their strengths and the geometry of the draw. Team competitions replace the path product with rubber-level aggregation: a tie is decided by singles and doubles rubbers that depend on who is nominated, which surface the host chooses, and how fatigue and doubles availability play out, followed by group or knockout advancement rules. The two settings share a settlement dependency on how the league designates each player's nationality and on who actually competes.

stages.name: Who counts: roster definition and nationality designation
stages.description: The contract population is the set of players the league designates as the nation's, which can differ from passport or residence: players competing as neutral athletes, switching allegiance or holding dual nationality are settlement edge cases. The roster for a draw also depends on entries and withdrawals before and after the draw.
stages.distribution: Discrete roster of 0-12 compatriots per draw; the designation uncertainty affects a handful of players but can dominate a small national group.

stages.name: Individual probabilities of reaching the stage
stages.description: Each compatriot has an individual probability of winning or reaching a stage, from the path simulation with surface-adjusted ratings, the draw and fatigue. These are marginals; the union cannot be built from them alone.
stages.distribution: Marginals ranging from under 1% for qualifiers to 20-40% for top players; very skewed across the roster with depth beyond the top two mattering little.

stages.name: Compatriot collisions in the bracket
stages.description: If two compatriots can meet before the stage, the meeting removes one with certainty. The probability that both reach the collision round and meet reduces the union probability relative to independence, and the effect depends on draw positions, which are random before the draw and fixed after.
stages.distribution: Pairwise collision probabilities by round, strongly dependent on bracket geometry; mass concentrated in rounds 2-3 for players seeded close together.

stages.name: Union and count aggregation
stages.description: The union probability is built from marginals and collision structure: P(at least one) is one minus the probability that all fail, with positive dependence from shared conditions (court speed, travel) and negative dependence from collisions. Count thresholds use the full distribution of the number of successes.
stages.distribution: Discrete count distribution on 0-2 at the final stage, 0-8 at earlier rounds; union saturates with roster depth.

stages.name: Team-competition rubber model
stages.description: Conditional stage (no team-competition series is listed live; apply only if one is listed). For a team tie, the outcome is the number of rubbers won: nominated singles players, a doubles pair, and the order. Captains choose the lineup, the host selects the surface and court speed, and fatigue across days alters the third rubber. The tie win probability needs the lineup distribution, not just top players' ratings.
stages.distribution: Discrete tie outcomes (2-0, 2-1, 1-2, 0-2) from rubber probabilities that are correlated through the host's surface and the lineup; the deciding doubles has the highest variance.

stages.name: Group advancement and settlement rules
stages.description: Conditional stage (no team-competition series is listed live; apply only if one is listed). Team competitions with a group phase use tie-break orders (ties won, rubbers, sets, games) and nationalities rules for eligibility; these determine advancement in close groups. The motivation of players to attend, and whether the event is an exhibition, adds a participation uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Rule-driven discrete advancement; the probability mass in tie-break resolution is small but decisive in close groups.

game_context_script.note: Nationality-count and team-advancement contracts are generated by tournament and tie structure, not by in-match game flow; match scripts matter only inside the rubber model through ratings.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume quantity: the outcome is a union or a count of players or rubbers, whose number is fixed by the format rather than forecast as a rate times opportunities.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion rate is separately defined for nationality or team markets; conversion is embedded in the individual path probabilities.

ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.label: Compatriot collision matrix by round
ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.mechanism: The probability that two players of the same nation meet before a given stage and so cannot both advance.
ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.rationale: The union probability of a nationality contract falls below the independent union by the collision term; the term depends on draw positions and the probability both survive to the meeting round.
ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.measurement: Run N=20000 bracket simulations using match win probabilities as-of draw publication (before the draw: resample draws respecting seeding rules). For nation c and stage s: U_sim = share of sims with at least one nation-c player reaching s; U_indep = 1 - prod_i(1 - p_i,s) with marginal p from the same sims; collision term = U_indep - U_sim >= 0. Also report P(pair meets) per pair and the earliest possible round from bracket sections. Nationality per ten.nationality_designation_status.
raw_data: draw positions, seeds, nationality (ioc/ official flag)
per-match win probabilities from the model
ten.compatriot_collision_matrix.why: Quantifies the structural dependence that reduces the union probability.

ten.nationality_designation_status.label: Nationality designation and neutral-status register
ten.nationality_designation_status.mechanism: Which players the league designates as the nation's, including neutral designations and allegiance switches.
ten.nationality_designation_status.rationale: The contract defers to the governing league's designation; players with neutral status or dual nationality can be inside or outside the nation's set, and that changes the union.
ten.nationality_designation_status.measurement: Register per player: designated nation as shown on the tournament draw sheet and ATP/WTA player profile (the contract defers to the 'Governing League'; use the draw-sheet flag at draw publication as the primary value and the ATP/WTA profile as the check), passport nation, neutral-athlete flag, date of last change; flag players whose designation differs across sources and treat them as a binary uncertain-membership case. No source exists for the probability that a designation changes before settlement, so it is carried as a scenario flag, not an estimated hazard (see nt_designation_source). As-of: draw publication.
raw_data: player nationality fields from draw sheet, ATP/WTA profile, passport
ten.nationality_designation_status.why: Settlement-critical for small national groups and neutral-status players.

ten.host_surface_selection.label: Host surface and court speed selection in team events
ten.host_surface_selection.mechanism: The host nation picks the surface and sometimes the court speed to favour its players in team ties.
ten.host_surface_selection.rationale: The rubber probabilities depend on the surface and pace; a host that picks a slow clay court changes which players are favoured relative to neutral ratings.
ten.host_surface_selection.measurement: From tie announcements record the surface, indoor/outdoor and pace descriptor; compute each nominated player's pace-adjusted rating (Elo + speed slope * pace) and the change in tie win probability against neutral-surface ratings. As-of: surface announcement (typically weeks before the tie). SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for pace data.
free_sources: ITF Davis Cup and BJK Cup announcements
ten.host_surface_selection.why: Conditional on a team-competition series being listed (none was found live); until then context only. Captures the home surface advantage as an explicit input rather than a crowd dummy.

ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.label: Team tie lineup distribution
ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.mechanism: The set of nominated singles players and doubles pair and the captain's likely choices.
ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.rationale: A tie result is determined by the lineup, which is announced late and depends on nominations, fitness and captain history.
ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.measurement: Probability distribution over lineups: P(player nominated) from nomination lists (usually 4-5 players); P(starts singles 1/2) from captain history and rankings; doubles pair from past ties and partnership record; rubber win probabilities from pace-adjusted ratings; simulate the tie (best of three or five rubbers). As-of: nomination list publication.
ten.team_tie_lineup_distribution.why: Conditional on a team-competition series being listed (none was found live); until then context only. Provides the lineup layer that individual ratings cannot supply.

ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.label: Group tie-break order and rubber results
ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.mechanism: The order of tie-breakers (ties, rubbers, sets, games) and the current group state decide advancement in close groups.
ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.rationale: Advancement in a group of three or four can come down to sets and games ratios, so the margin of wins matters, not only the win.
ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.measurement: Encode event rules (ordered tie-break criteria), current group table, remaining ties; simulate remaining ties with rubber distributions and compute advancement; flag cases where games ratio decides (probability > 5%). As-of: after each tie.
ten.team_group_tiebreak_rules.why: Conditional on a team-competition series being listed (none was found live); until then context only. Settles the cases where winners are tied and margin matters.

ten.home_slam_depth_prior.label: Home-nation depth prior at home majors
ten.home_slam_depth_prior.mechanism: Historical distribution of the number of home-nation players reaching each round at their own major.
ten.home_slam_depth_prior.rationale: A calibration prior for union contracts (such as 1+ Americans in the final) that checks the union model against history.
ten.home_slam_depth_prior.measurement: For each nation and major, compute frequency of at least one home player reaching R16, QF, SF, F over the last 15 editions with decay half-life 6 years; blend with the path-model value using an initial weight of 0.3 that is a placeholder to be fitted on held-out editions (not calibrated); report by tour. As-of: before event. Because a historical home-progress frequency partly re-encodes the strength the model already captures, use it only as an out-of-sample calibration check on the union probability, not as an extra driver inside the model.
raw_data: nationality by player and round reached
ten.home_slam_depth_prior.why: Provides an empirical check on union probabilities for home-nation contracts.

ten.nationality_field_strength.reason: The roster and the individual marginals are needed, but as an output of the path simulation rather than a separate measured variable.

ten.path_difficulty_sim.reason: Supplies each compatriot's marginal; must be combined with the collision term to give a union.

ten.bracket_correlation.reason: The dependence among compatriots is the whole difference from a sum of marginals; define it through the collision matrix.

ten.team_event_structure.reason: Rubber structure and lineups drive team ties, but no team-competition series (Davis Cup, BJK Cup, United Cup, Laver Cup) was found live, so this is conditional context, not primary; the live nationality contracts depend on the collision matrix and designation register instead.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Underlies rubber and path probabilities but does not include the pace selected by the host.

ten.home_crowd.reason: Home crowd effects in individual tennis are small and mostly proxied by surface choice; the evidence for a separable crowd factor is thin.

ten.pre_draw_field.reason: Entries and withdrawals define the roster of compatriots; vintage matters.

ten.fitness.reason: Injury state of compatriots changes the roster and path probabilities; main uncertainty for national groups with few strong players.

m.rules_text.reason: The designation rule and the union versus count wording are the contract; read per series.

ten.motivation.reason: Participation in team events such as Laver Cup or Davis Cup depends on stakes and exhibition status; hard to quantify.

interactions.mechanism: The union loss from a collision depends on how likely both compatriots are to survive to the meeting round, so the correction is large for two strong seeds in the same quarter and negligible for a strong seed and a qualifier.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated unions with and without enforcing the collision, by seed pairing class.

interactions.mechanism: A single player whose designation is uncertain can switch the contract from near-zero to material probability for a small national group, a threshold effect around the status of that player.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the contract probability under each status assignment for groups with fewer than three players.

interactions.mechanism: The surface chosen by the host changes the strength ranking of the nominated players, and the lineup determines which of those players are exposed, so the two multiply in the tie win probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate ties with the lineup fixed and with the surface effect removed and compare tie win probabilities to historical home advantage.

interactions.mechanism: In a group with tied win counts, advancement depends on rubbers, sets and games ratios, so the margin of victory in the final tie has a disproportionate effect on advancement.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate groups with ties and measure how often margin criteria decide, compared with historical groups.

interactions.mechanism: A collision between compatriots removes one of them only if both reach the meeting round healthy; an injury or withdrawal of one compatriot before that round converts the would-be collision into a walkover for the other, so the union loss from a collision shrinks as the injury probability of either rises. The effect is largest when two strong compatriots are drawn into the same quarter.
interactions.how_to_test: Historical draws with two or more compatriots in one quarter: compare observed union rate against the simulation with and without a withdrawal-hazard term by fitness-flag status.

nonlinearities.why: Union probability is one minus the product of failures, so each extra compatriot adds a smaller increment, especially when the top compatriot has a high individual probability.
The dependence appears at the first round where two compatriots can meet; before it the union is close to independent, after it the correction is exact and large.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in tie win probability over rubbers
nonlinearities.why: A best-of-three tie amplifies rubber edges: the tie win probability of the better team rises faster than the rubber win probability for edges above about 55%.

contract.settlement_definition: One live series, KXATPACES, with recovered rules: 'If Taylor Fritz records at least 19 total match aces in the full match of the ... match ..., then the market resolves to Yes' (floor_strike 18.5, so each market is an 'N+' rung on one player's full-match ace count). An ace is defined as 'A serve that lands in the service box and is not touched by the receiving player ... resulting in an immediate point for the server'. A match that never starts resolves to a fair price. On retirement 'all markets will resolve based on the statistics officially completed and recorded prior to the cancellation or discontinuation of the match', so the count is truncated and unreached rungs settle No rather than void. No double-fault series is listed. The text does not name the statistics provider, does not contain the postponement sentence used by the game-level series, and is silent on whether tiebreak and match-tiebreak serves count (they are serves, so presumably yes).

rules_evidence.quote: records at least 19 total match aces in the full match
rules_evidence.establishes: The settled quantity is one player's ace count over the full match against an 'at least N' rung (floor 18.5).

rules_evidence.quote: If a retirement occurs, all markets will resolve based on the statistics officially completed and recorded prior to the cancellation or discontinuation of the match.
rules_evidence.establishes: A retirement truncates the count and settles every rung on aces recorded so far; rungs not yet reached settle No, so retirement hazard is a direct downside for the over side.

rules_evidence.quote: A serve that lands in the service box and is not touched by the receiving player
rules_evidence.establishes: The ace definition is the standard one (untouched legal serve); let serves and faults are not aces, and a touched serve winner is not an ace.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction: 'at least N' rungs from one player's count (19+ sampled); rungs are nested, so their probabilities must be monotone in N.
Retirement: truncation at the officially recorded count; a retirement by either player ends the server's exposure, so the opponent's retirement hazard also lowers the named player's over probability.

Source of truth: 'statistics officially completed and recorded' without a named provider; official ATP statistics and broadcaster or vendor counts can differ by one or two aces (ac_source_disagreement).
Postponement: unlike the game-level series, the sampled ace text has no postponement sentence; whether a suspended match continuing the next day is still the same market is not stated.

Double faults and match totals: no double-fault or match-total ace series is listed, so stage s5 (double-fault pressure) and the pair-correlation gap are conditional on such a series being listed; they stay as mechanism content for the shared first-serve factor.
contract.settlement_data_source: 'Statistics officially completed and recorded' (provider not named); presumably the ATP/Slam official match statistics.

mechanism.summary: An ace count is the number of service points on which a given server is not touched by the returner, so it is a sum over the points he serves of a rare event whose per-point probability depends on the server's pace and placement, the returner's reach and position, the court and the air. The count is therefore rate times exposure. Exposure is the number of service points the player serves, which depends on the number of games played, on how long each service game lasts (quick holds use fewer points than deuce-heavy ones) and on whether tiebreaks are played, and it is endogenous: a big server who holds quickly serves fewer points per game. The rate is the product of first-serve in-percentage and ace probability given first-serve in, plus small second-serve ace and double-fault terms, and varies from day to day beyond binomial noise because first-serve percentage and serve speed move together with form and conditions. Double faults mirror this through second-serve policy and pressure. The settlement layer is the official count and its truncation at retirement.

stages.name: Expected service points as the exposure
stages.description: Every ace needs a service point, so the first object is the number of points the named player serves. It is the number of service games times points per game, plus the player's share of tiebreak points. Points per game is not constant: a game held to love takes four points, a deuce game six or more, so the average depends on the spw and the returner.
stages.distribution: Discrete exposure around 60-110 service points in a best-of-three and roughly 90-180 in a best-of-five (the sampled KXATPACES market is a Wimbledon men's match, so best-of-five); mixture over match scenarios (straight-set win, loss, three sets, tiebreaks) with a heavy right tail from long matches.

stages.name: First-serve in-rate and ace probability given first serve in
stages.description: The per-point ace probability is the product of the share of first serves that land in and the probability that a first serve in is untouched. A player who takes pace off to land more first serves lowers the ace chance given in; a player who hits for pace raises both ace probability and fault risk, so the trade-off is non-monotone.
stages.distribution: Two linked Bernoulli rates (illustrative ranges, to be estimated from data rather than taken as established: in% roughly 0.55-0.70, ace given in a few percent to about a third for elite servers); product has a limited range with a negative trade-off between the two components.

stages.name: Returner and direction effects
stages.description: Aces depend on the returner: reach, return position, handedness and tendency to stand deep. A tall left-handed server using the wide serve on the ad court against a weak backhand return produces more aces than the average. The pair interaction is strong because the ace is the returner's failure to touch the ball.
stages.distribution: Rate varies by factor 2 across returners for the same server; interaction with serve direction mix.

stages.name: Court, air and condition shifts
stages.description: Fast courts, high altitude (thin air reduces drag), indoor stillness and the ball in use all raise ace probability; wind adds variance and side-dependent effects. These are event-level shifts that apply to every match at that event and week, so the event's own history of ace rates is the best predictor.
stages.distribution: Event-level location shifts of 10-40% in ace rate; wind is additional noise with side asymmetry.

stages.name: Day-level variation, double-fault pressure and overdispersion
stages.description: Ace counts are more variable than a binomial: a day with a hot first serve yields many more. Double faults come from second-serve risk and pressure at critical points; both counts share the day-level first-serve factor, producing overdispersion relative to a constant-rate count.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative-binomial or beta-binomial) with a variance-to-mean ratio above one that is a parameter to estimate (an assumed 1.5-3 is unsourced); zero-inflation small.

stages.name: Counting rule and truncation
stages.description: The settled count is whatever the official statistics record: KXATPACES defines an ace as an untouched legal serve and resolves on 'statistics officially completed and recorded'. Let-cord serves, challenged calls and foot faults can shift the recorded number by one or two, and a retirement stops the count at that moment and settles every rung on it, so unreached rungs lose. These rules matter most for ladder rungs close to the median and for players with a high retirement hazard.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete discrepancies of 0-2 aces between sources; truncation concentrates in retiring or injured players.

availability_news.note: General pre-match fitness, withdrawal signals and the match retirement base rate truncate or shift the counted exposure; serve-specific injury information (shoulder, wrist) and in-event speed drops remain unavailable from a free structured source and are carried in ac_injury_gap.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching on serve tactics (direction patterns, second-serve risk) exists but is not observable before the match; the effect is reflected in the player's own direction mix and double-fault history.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and schedule shift serve speed by small amounts relative to the exposure and the opponent effects; no standalone variable is justified at the match level.

ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.label: Service-points exposure by match scenario
ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.mechanism: The player's service points are a mixture over match scenarios and depend on points per service game.
ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.rationale: The existing match-length input is an expectation; the ace distribution depends on the full exposure distribution and its correlation with the ace rate (a player serving well wins quickly and serves fewer points).
ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.measurement: For each player compute N = sum over scenarios s (straight-set win/loss, 3-set, 4-set, 5-set, with and without tiebreaks) of P(s) * (service games_s * E[points per game | spw, rpw] + tiebreak serve points); E[points per game] from the point-score Markov chain (about 5.3 at spw 0.65). Keep the scenario weights from the set-count distribution and from hold probabilities. As-of: before match. Add a retirement scenario: with probability P(ret) from ten.retirement_base_rate (by tour, round, best_of, pre-match fitness flag) the match stops at game g drawn from the retirement-timing distribution, so N is truncated to the service points served before g; the count at retirement is then compared with each rung under ten.retirement_settlement_rules.
ten.service_points_scenario_mixture.why: Provides the exposure distribution, including its dependence on holds, as the base of the count.

ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.label: Serve direction mix versus returner weakness
ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.mechanism: Ace probability depends on direction (wide, body, T) and side and on the returner's weaker wing.
ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.rationale: The pair interaction is where most of the variance in ace rate sits; direction frequencies are player-specific and known.
ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.measurement: From charted points compute the server's share of wide/body/T by side and the ace rate by direction, and the returner's unreturned share by direction; expected ace probability = sum over direction of share_server * (ace rate by direction adjusted by returner weakness); shrink with n/(n+80). Coverage is limited to charted matches.
raw_data: serve direction and outcome per point
ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner.why: Represents the pair-specific channel that raw ace rates miss.

ten.line_calling_regime.label: Line-calling regime and foot-fault enforcement
ten.line_calling_regime.mechanism: Electronic line calling versus human line judges and foot-fault enforcement change which serves count as aces or faults.
ten.line_calling_regime.rationale: Systematic differences in service-box calls can shift ace and fault counts by small amounts; regime differs by event and year.
ten.line_calling_regime.measurement: Event-year flags for electronic line calling and for line judges; estimate the regime effect on ace rate by regressing ace per service point on the regime flag with player and surface effects; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the event list by year.
ten.line_calling_regime.why: Handles an officiating-regime variable that changes counts without changing play.

ten.second_serve_risk_policy.label: Second-serve risk policy
ten.second_serve_risk_policy.mechanism: The double-fault rate depends on how aggressively a player hits the second serve, which varies with the returner and the score.
ten.second_serve_risk_policy.rationale: Double-fault counts are not just noise: players who hit big second serves against aggressive returners fault more.
ten.second_serve_risk_policy.measurement: Per player, estimate P(DF | second serve) as a function of returner aggression (share of second serves attacked), score pressure (break point flag), and age; shrink with n/(n+60); output expected DF rate against this returner. As-of: day before the match.
free_sources: Sackmann serve counts (df and second serve counts)
ten.second_serve_risk_policy.why: Provides a mechanism for double-fault rate variation beyond a player average.

ten.first_serve_speed_trend.label: First-serve speed trend within and across matches
ten.first_serve_speed_trend.mechanism: Serve speed in the current event and its decay over the match predict ace rate.
ten.first_serve_speed_trend.rationale: Pre-event speed averages mask injuries and form; in-event speed from earlier rounds is a direct indicator of the current serve state.
ten.first_serve_speed_trend.measurement: Per player compute mean first-serve speed in the last two matches and in the previous 10 matches (if published), z-score vs career; expected ace rate adjusted by elasticity beta estimated per player; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for availability of serve-speed data outside the majors.
ten.first_serve_speed_trend.why: Adds a state variable for serve health that is not in the static physical profile.

ten.ace_opp_adjusted.reason: The core rate; must be opponent-adjusted using returner effects, not raw ace rate.

ten.match_length_expectation.reason: Exposure driver but only the mean; replaced in function by the scenario mixture which adds the distribution.

ten.first_serve.reason: First-serve in% and ace given in jointly define the rate; the trade-off between them is the interesting part.

ten.first_serve_in_variance.reason: Day variation in first-serve percentage drives overdispersion; only knowable in retrospect, so it informs the variance parameter.

ten.serve_profile_physical.reason: Speed and height give a prior for young or returning players; good for cold starts.

ten.venue_speed_history.reason: Event-level ace rate history is the best proxy for court and ball conditions.

ten.altitude.reason: Real but only matters at a handful of venues; effectively captured by the event's own history.

ten.wind_indoor.reason: Indoor flag is deterministic; wind needs a forecast and acts mostly on variance.

ten.double_fault_pressure.reason: Double-fault rate under pressure is a component of the second-serve risk policy; the new definition adds returner dependence.

ten.ace_settlement_source.reason: Source differences of one or two aces matter at the median rung; must be nailed down.

ten.aces_df.reason: For aces the opponent-adjusted ten.ace_opp_adjusted supersedes the raw rate, but the raw double-fault rate and serve-speed fields have no other existing input and are the only existing source for the double-fault side; keep as the DF ingredient paired with second_serve_risk_policy rather than as a duplicate.

ten.ball_type_pressure.reason: Ball brand effects are event-level and already in venue history; direct data are sparse.

ten.return_style_rally.reason: Returner reach and position are decisive for aces; coarse proxy until direction data are available.

ten.ace_count_distribution.reason: The ladder requires the whole distribution; per-player dispersion must be estimated and shrunk.

interactions.mechanism: Expected aces equal rate times service points, but the two are negatively correlated: a server with a high ace rate holds quickly, uses fewer points per game and wins faster, so the product is lower than the naive product for big servers.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised ace counts with rate times exposure computed with and without conditioning on match scenario for high-ace-rate servers.

interactions.mechanism: Thin air reduces drag so the ball carries pace; players with high serve speed gain more in absolute ace probability than slower servers.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress ace rate on altitude interacted with serve speed percentile.

interactions.mechanism: Wind lowers first-serve in-percentage on the windward end, which reduces aces there and raises double faults; the effect shows up as extra variance, not a mean shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare variance of ace counts across outdoor wind bins and indoor matches.

interactions.mechanism: A drop in first-serve speed over the last matches signals fatigue or an arm problem; a hurt server tends to protect the first serve (fewer aces) while the safer second serve may or may not keep the double-fault rate down, so the sign of the double-fault response depends on how the player adapts. The link is conditional on a speed-drop regime, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Split player-matches by the first-serve speed z-score (below -1 versus above) and compare ace rate and double-fault rate per service point, conditioning on opponent return aggression; test whether the double-fault slope differs by regime.

interactions.mechanism: Raising first-serve pace raises ace given in but lowers in-percentage and adds second-serve points where double faults occur; aces and double faults move together with a non-monotone net effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot aces and double faults per service point against first-serve in% across player-matches and check for an interior optimum.

nonlinearities.shape: concave trade-off between in-percentage and ace probability
nonlinearities.why: Ace probability given a first serve in rises with pace while in-percentage falls, so aces per service point has an interior maximum rather than increasing with pace.
A match that goes to a fifth set adds 25-40 service points for each player, so exposure is bimodal in best-of-five and the count distribution inherits a heavy right tail.
Ace probability rises with altitude but flattens beyond moderate elevations because court and ball conditions dominate once the air is thin.

contract.settlement_definition: Four event definitions share this archetype. KXATPCOMPETE settles Yes if the named player 'competes in the 2026 US Open men's singles tennis tournament' (participation in a named event, with 'competes' undefined in the sample: entry, appearing in the draw, or playing a ball). KXATPRETURN settles Yes if the player 'competes in an ATP Match after May 19, 2026 and before September 1, 2026', with a note that the US Open counts, so it is a time-to-return event inside a closed window. KXATPRETIRE settles Yes if the player announces retirement before 2027, with the note that the retirement 'must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to 2027'. KXWTASERENA settles Yes if 'Serena Williams competes in any WTA official tournament in 2026', a comeback from completed retirement with no secondary text. None of the sampled texts states what happens on a walkover, a first-point retirement, or a late withdrawal, nor the named source of truth.

rules_evidence.quote: If Jannik Sinner competes in the 2026 US Open men's singles tennis tournament, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Yes requires competing in the named event; the rules text defines no minimum (one match, one point) and no treatment of a walkover or withdrawal after the draw.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: The retirement must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to 2027.
rules_evidence.establishes: Only an announcement of a retirement effective immediately or before 2027 settles Yes; an announcement of a retirement effective in 2027 or later fails the note, while a farewell season that ends before 2027 would still satisfy it.

rules_evidence.quote: If Carlos Alcaraz competes in an ATP Match after May 19, 2026 and before September 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The return window is closed on both ends with a stated start date; any ATP match inside the window counts.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: The US Open Tennis Championships is part of the ATP Tour and therefore would count as an ATP Match for the purposes of this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Majors are explicitly included as ATP matches for this series, which sets the calendar of eligible events.

rules_evidence.quote: If Serena Williams competes in any WTA official tournament in 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A retired player's return to any WTA official tournament within a calendar year; 'competes' and 'WTA official tournament' (Slams, WTA 125, doubles) are undefined.

variants_and_edge_cases: A walkover versus a played match: whether a player entered but withdrawing before the first ball 'competes' is not stated for KXATPCOMPETE; the match-level rules treat a pre-start walkover as non-occurrence, which points to No but is not confirmed.
In-match retirement after the first ball: competing has plainly started, so a player who retires in the first round likely counts for COMPETE and RETURN, but the rules do not say so.

Retirement announcement scope: an announcement made before 2027 that the player will retire at the end of 2027 does not meet the 'effective immediately or prior to 2027' note; a statement of 'considering retirement' is not an announcement.

Time windows with clock ambiguity: window endpoints (May 19 and September 1) are dates without a time zone or timestamp, and the issued-date condition 'after Issuance' used by the major series is not visible here.

Eligible-event scope for KXATPRETURN: the note makes the US Open an ATP Match explicitly, but ATP Challenger, team-event ties (Davis Cup, Laver Cup), exhibitions, Olympic and qualifying matches are not addressed; ten.eligible_event_calendar must be built for the ATP Tour main-draw events only until scope is clarified (rp_atp_match_scope).

Verification level: the rules text was read for all four series, but 'competes' is undefined, the source of truth is unnamed and the announcement channel is not visible, so the contract is only partially verified.

Return from completed retirement (KXWTASERENA): the player is not injured but retired, so the path runs through a re-entry decision, anti-doping re-registration notice and a wildcard or protected-ranking entry; whether doubles, a WTA 125 event or a Grand Slam (ITF-sanctioned, on the WTA calendar) is a 'WTA official tournament' is not stated.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; ATP Tour official draws, results and public statements are the natural sources (not verified).

mechanism.summary: These contracts are not about a match; they ask whether a person takes an action inside a window, and the action is gated by health, calendar and decision. For a return or participation contract the chain is: the player's current physical state and its recovery timeline, the set of events in the window that he is eligible to enter, his or his team's decision to enter given points, prize money and fitness risk, a withdrawal hazard between entry deadline and first ball, and the definition of what counts as competing. For a retirement announcement the chain is a hazard over career stage: age, results trend, injury burden, financial and personal factors, and the habit of announcing at certain moments (end of season, a major, a farewell tour). The structure is a time-to-event process with a deadline and calendar-dependent opportunities, so the right object is a survival curve rather than a rate, and the information that moves it (an injury report, a withdrawal, a press statement) arrives in discrete jumps whose timestamp matters as much as their content.

stages.name: Physical state and recovery timeline
stages.description: The player's current health and any injury layoff set the earliest feasible return date. Recovery time depends on injury type and whether surgery was performed; public statements and training evidence narrow a wide prior. Returns are rarely earlier than stated and often later, so the timeline is right-skewed.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed time-to-return distribution (log-normal-like) conditional on injury class; Kaplan-Meier from historical layoffs with censoring for players who do not return within a season.

stages.name: Eligible events and entry pathways
stages.description: A return or participation needs a place in a draw. Entry depends on ranking versus cutoff, protected ranking, wildcard or special exemption, and acceptance list deadlines, so even a healthy player may be unable to enter a given event. The calendar within the window decides the number of attempts.
stages.distribution: Discrete set of opportunities with heterogeneous entry probability; a player under cutoff has near-zero odds without a wildcard.

stages.name: Entry decision and incentives
stages.description: Given health and eligibility, the team decides whether to commit: rankings points to defend, prize money (including first-round pay for losers), event importance and the risk of aggravating the injury. High-incentive events such as Slams make injured players start more often than ordinary events.
stages.distribution: Binary decision per event with probability rising with incentive and falling with injury severity; strongly event-dependent.

stages.name: Withdrawal and walkover hazard between entry and first ball
stages.description: After entry the player can withdraw until the draw and even after the order of play; each interval has its own hazard and each has different information (practice sessions, press conferences). The 'competes' definition determines whether a withdrawal after the draw ends the contract at No.
stages.distribution: Hazard concentrated in the 48 hours before the first scheduled match; withdrawal probability increases with recent layoff and reported complaint.

stages.name: Retirement announcement hazard
stages.description: For the retirement contract the process is different: a hazard of announcing retirement as a function of age, career length, ranking trajectory, injury load and personal statements. Announcements cluster around the end of the season, after major tournaments and at farewell events, and are rarely made out of a clear sky for top players still winning.
stages.distribution: Low-probability annual hazard for most players, rising past 33-35 and with ranking decline; right tail for injury-forced announcements.

stages.name: Settlement definition and source
stages.description: What counts as competing, which data source decides, and the time of resolution determine edge cases: a walkover in round one, a retirement after one game, an announcement with a delayed effective date. The retirement base rate and match-level settlement wording matter for how in-event outcomes are recorded.
stages.distribution: Definition-driven discrete edge cases; probability mass small but systematic around Slam first rounds.

stages.name: Return from completed retirement
stages.description: KXWTASERENA asks whether a player who has already retired competes in any WTA official tournament in 2026. The chain is: a personal decision to return, an anti-doping re-registration with advance notice that fixes the earliest eligible date, an entry route without a ranking (wildcard, special exemption or a doubles slot with a partner), and then the first match before the window closes. Each link is observable only through announcements, and the notice period alone can make the event impossible late in the year.
stages.distribution: Near-degenerate at zero absent a public re-entry step; after a step, a time-to-event hazard truncated by the window end, with the notice period acting as a hard lower bound on time to first match.

opponent_matchup.note: Participation and retirement-announcement outcomes do not depend on an opponent; the only opponent-dependent element is first-round walkover timing, which is part of the withdrawal hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach and team decisions affect scheduling but are not observable as separate variables; their effect passes through public statements and the entry decision captured by incentives and news.

environment.note: Weather, heat and rain delays do not decide whether a player enters, returns or announces retirement within a window; they affect match timing only, and in-match retirement conditions are not part of these three contracts.

game_context_script.note: No game script is involved; a participation or announcement contract is a calendar event rather than a match state, and the in-match retirement is covered under the availability inputs.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume count; the quantity is binary within a window, and the number of eligible events is an opportunity set handled under the calendar input.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion rate exists beyond the entry decision probability, which is covered under incentive and availability inputs.

ten.layoff_survival_curve.label: Layoff survival curve by injury class
ten.layoff_survival_curve.mechanism: Time-to-return distribution after an injury layoff, conditional on injury class and public statements.
ten.layoff_survival_curve.rationale: The catalog has a generic comeback input but a time-to-return contract needs a survival curve with censoring; the key is the probability of returning before a fixed date given days already missed.
ten.layoff_survival_curve.measurement: Enumerate every gap >=30 days in a ranked top-100 player's match history (gap start = last match date). Event = first match after the gap; players with no further match by the as-of date are right-censored. Injury class from manual coding of press at gap start (missing = 'unknown'). Kaplan-Meier per class; conditional curve S(t+d)/S(d) for d days already elapsed; shrink class hazard to pooled with n/(n+20). Statement types shift the hazard via a Cox coefficient estimated on coded cases. As-of: day of market.
raw_data: injury label and surgery flag (manual coding)
ten.layoff_survival_curve.why: [Applies to KXATPRETURN and KXATPCOMPETE (not KXATPRETIRE)] Gives the probability of a return in a fixed window as a survival value rather than an average layoff length.

ten.eligible_event_calendar.label: Eligible event calendar inside the window
ten.eligible_event_calendar.mechanism: The number and type of events a player can enter before the deadline set the number of chances to return or participate.
ten.eligible_event_calendar.rationale: A return before a date is a union across entry opportunities with different entry and incentive probabilities.
ten.eligible_event_calendar.measurement: For player i and window ending T: events e with entry deadline after as-of and start <= T. P(eligible_e) = 1 if rank <= last direct acceptance in last 3 editions, else historical share of such ranks receiving wildcard/protected entry (shrunk n/(n+10)). P(commit_e | eligible) = player's share over last 24 months of eligible same-category events actually entered, shrunk n/(n+8) to category mean. P(return by T) = 1 - prod_e(1 - P(eligible_e)P(commit_e)P(start_e | enter)). Challenger/exhibition carried separately.
raw_data: calendar with entry deadlines, category, surface, points
ten.eligible_event_calendar.why: Converts a time window into a count of chances with explicit entry deadlines.

ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.label: Protected ranking, wildcard and cutoff pathway
ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.mechanism: Whether a returning player can enter depends on ranking cutoff, protected-ranking use and wildcard probability.
ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.rationale: A healthy but low-ranked returnee needs a protected ranking or a wildcard; both are discrete and time-limited.
ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.measurement: Per player and event: rank_now, protected_rank (value, expiry, uses left) from tour announcements, cutoff_e = worst rank directly accepted in each of the last 3 editions (median). P(eligible) = 1 if min(rank_now, protected_rank if valid) <= cutoff_e; otherwise wildcard probability = historical share of wildcard places given to players with the same status (former top-10, home nation, ex-champion) divided by their entries, shrunk n/(n+10). As-of: entry list publication.
raw_data: rank, protected ranking value/expiry, event direct-acceptance cutoffs by edition
ten.protected_ranking_and_entry_pathway.why: Provides the entry gate that depends on rules, not on health.

ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.label: Withdrawal hazard timeline from entry deadline to first ball
ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.mechanism: Probability of withdrawal at each interval: before the draw, after the draw before order of play, before the first match.
ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.rationale: The hazard is time-varying and clusters near the start; intervals carry different information, which determines when a market should move.
ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.measurement: Unit = (player listed at entry deadline). Intervals: I1 entry deadline to draw, I2 draw to order-of-play, I3 order-of-play to first ball. Hazard_k = P(withdraw in I_k | still in at start of I_k) by discrete-time logistic with covariates event category (Slam/Masters/500/250/Challenger), rank band (1-10,11-30,31-60,61+), age bin, days since last match; ridge equivalent to n/(n+30). Training data only from own-captured snapshots plus archived lists; as-of = snapshot vintage time.
free_sources: Entry list and draw archives (Wikipedia, official sites)
raw_data: entry list snapshots, draw, order of play, results
ten.withdrawal_hazard_timeline.why: [Applies to KXATPCOMPETE and KXATPRETURN (not KXATPRETIRE)] Provides the interval hazards for participation contracts that vanish in a final-state dataset.

ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.label: Retirement announcement hazard by age and rank
ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.mechanism: Annual and within-year hazard of announcing retirement given age, career length, ranking trend and injuries.
ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.rationale: The retirement contract is a low-probability tail event that depends on structured career variables and on announcement habits.
ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.measurement: From historical career-end records for players with careers of at least eight years: hazard by age bin (30-31, 32-33, ..., 38+), rank band, injury layoff flag, prior announcements; discrete-time logistic; shrink to pooled with n/(n+25); output the probability of an announcement effective by the deadline. As-of: before the decision date. Avoid survivorship: the at-risk set must include every player with an eight-plus-year career in each age bin whether or not he later announced (active players censored at the as-of date), not only players found on retirement lists; the announcement date itself is taken from the dated statement, not the final match.
raw_data: player birth date, last match, announcement date, rank history
ten.retirement_announcement_hazard.why: [Applies to KXATPRETIRE only] Gives a baseline hazard for retirement-announcement markets.

ten.unretirement_reentry_status.label: Re-entry status of a retired player (testing-pool notice and entry route)
ten.unretirement_reentry_status.mechanism: A player who has retired can only compete again after re-registering for anti-doping testing with advance notice and obtaining a main-draw place by wildcard or special/protected ranking.
ten.unretirement_reentry_status.rationale: For a comeback-from-retirement contract the binding constraint is administrative and personal, not physical recovery: the WADA Code return-from-retirement rule requires written notice to the anti-doping authority months before competing, and with no ranking the player needs wildcards; a public notice is a near-necessary leading indicator that sharply separates a near-zero probability from a material one. Subtle: notice lists may not be public, and doubles or exhibition play can precede singles.
ten.unretirement_reentry_status.measurement: State variable as of the market timestamp with values {no public re-entry step, testing-pool re-registration reported (date), wildcard or protected-ranking entry announced (event, date), entered in an acceptance list}; earliest eligible competition date = notice date + required notice period (six months under the WADA Code rule, to be checked against the current ITIA Tennis Anti-Doping Programme); P(compete by window end) = 0 before the earliest eligible date, otherwise a hazard estimated from historical un-retirements (e.g. Clijsters, Hingis, Wozniacki) with n<20 so shrink heavily toward a judgemental prior.
free_sources: ITIA announcements and Tennis Anti-Doping Programme rules
ten.unretirement_reentry_status.why: KXWTASERENA settles Yes only if a retired player competes in a WTA official tournament in 2026; without a re-entry step the probability is near zero regardless of fitness.

interactions.mechanism: Return time and event opportunities interact: a player expected back in four weeks can only return at an event whose entry deadline falls after he is cleared, so a slow recovery near a deadline removes a chance entirely.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute historical P(return by T) conditional on whether any entry deadline fell inside the feasible recovery window.

interactions.mechanism: A returning player below the entry cutoff enters only through a protected ranking or wildcard, a binary gate; above it, incentives determine the decision, so the effect of incentives is zero below the gate.
interactions.how_to_test: Split return outcomes by whether rank was inside the direct acceptance cutoff and compare responses to incentive proxies.

interactions.mechanism: Injury raises the retirement announcement hazard most for older players with long careers, because the cost of rehab is higher and the remaining horizon shorter.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate announcement hazard by age with and without an injury-layoff flag and test the interaction.

interactions.mechanism: A press statement that changes the stated plan switches the participation hazard from the base state to a near-certain state; signals before the statement raise the hazard continuously while the statement itself jumps it.
interactions.how_to_test: Align withdrawals to the timing of practice signals and statements and compare hazard before and after each.

interactions.mechanism: The contract outcome after a post-draw withdrawal depends on the definition of competing, so the hazard timeline is relevant only conditional on the rule that treats a withdrawal after the draw as No.
interactions.how_to_test: Enumerate historical post-draw withdrawals of listed players and compute implied outcome under each reading.

nonlinearities.why: The probability of announcing retirement in a year rises slowly through the early thirties and steeply after about 35, so a linear age term misses the late-career acceleration.
Recovery time is bounded below by medical constraints but has a long right tail, so the probability of return by a date moves slowly as the date approaches and then jumps after clearance.

nonlinearities.shape: jump in hazard close to first ball
nonlinearities.why: Practice and press signals have almost no information weeks ahead but raise withdrawal probability sharply in the final 24 hours before play, so their effect is strongly time-varying.

contract.settlement_definition: Three settled families. Year-end rank contracts (KXATP1RANK, KXWTA1RANK, KXATPT5RANK) settle on the published rankings: 'If Taylor Fritz is the #1 ranked on the PIF ATP singles rankings on Dec 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET', using 'the most recently published PIF ATP Rankings available at the time of resolution', so the settlement is the last published weekly list, not a points total computed on that date. Major-title contracts (KXATPGRANDSLAM, KXWTAGRANDSLAM) settle Yes if the named player 'wins a tennis major (the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon, or the U.S. Open) after Issuance and before Dec 31, 2027', a union over the four majors of 2027 plus any remaining 2026 major at issuance. The cumulative contract (KXATPNOVAK25) requires a named player's 25th career major singles title before 2028 and counts singles only, so it also depends on his current count. No sampled text covers a player's retirement, withdrawal, or disqualification inside a major. Finals-qualification contracts (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL) settle Yes if the named player 'qualifies for the 2026 Nitto ATP Singles Finals' (or WTA Singles Finals), and a qualified player who does not compete still settles Yes; whether a promoted alternate counts as qualified is not stated. Two further major series: KXTENNISMAJORDJOKOVIC ('If Novak Djokovic wins a tennis major ... before Dec 31, 2025') is a one-player union over the 2025 majors (window closed before today's date), and KXATPGRANDSLAMFIELD settles Yes 'If any man other than Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner wins a tennis major ... before Dec 31, 2026', the complement of the two named players winning every remaining major; neither has secondary text.

variants_and_edge_cases: The ranking is the most recently published list, and ATP and WTA weeks without events may not publish; the Dec 31, 2026 12:00 PM ET snapshot is a Thursday, so the settlement list is probably the one issued after the final tournament, not a date-stamped calculation (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED publication calendar).

Window start for the major contracts is 'after Issuance', whose timestamp is not in the sample; a major that finished between issuance and today would count, and the window closes at 'before Dec 31, 2027' so only the 2027 majors remain after today's date (Nov 2026).

Cumulative contract: 'his 25th career major' depends on the count at issuance (a count of 24 at issuance is outside knowledge, not stated in the rules text); a title already won since issuance would shift the target, and retirement or a mid-tournament withdrawal ends the path.

Top-5 contract: a threshold on rank rather than a unique winner, so ties in points are broken by the governing league rules (not visible), and a rank of 5 versus 6 depends on small margins around the cutoff.

Finals qualification (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL, now filed here with rules text): Yes if the named player 'qualifies' for the ATP/WTA singles Finals, and 'If player qualifies but does not compete, the market resolves to Yes'. Not stated: whether an alternate who is promoted after a withdrawal counts as having qualified, the qualification cut-off date, and the ATP rule (outside knowledge, to be checked in the rulebook) that a current-year Grand Slam champion ranked 9-20 in the Race takes the 8th place.

Verification level: rules text was read for all ten series, but Top-5 and #1 tie-break rules, the issuance timestamp (sr_issuance_timestamp), the publication calendar and the alternate/Slam-champion qualification rules are not visible, so the contract is only partially verified.

Field and single-season major contracts (KXATPGRANDSLAMFIELD, KXTENNISMAJORDJOKOVIC): no secondary text, no 'after Issuance' clause and no withdrawal rule; the field contract pays Yes on one non-Alcaraz/Sinner title among the remaining majors, so it depends on the joint champion distribution per event (both named players' participation and the strength of the rest of the field), not on either player's marginal alone. All majors inside both windows (2025; 2026, last major the US Open in September) have been played by November 2026, so these series are effectively decided.

mechanism.summary: These contracts are aggregates over a finite remaining calendar, so the central object is the horizon: what can still change before the settlement date. In early November a year-end ranking is nearly determined by the points already earned and by a small number of remaining events (the final Masters and the Finals; team events such as the Davis Cup finals and Laver Cup award no ATP/WTA ranking points and matter only through whether players skip or play point-bearing events), so the question is whether the remaining maximum swing can overturn the current gap, and the probability moves in a threshold fashion as the lead approaches the size of that swing. A long-horizon major contract is different: it is a union of independent but correlated four-tournament lotteries, in which each player's probability is the chance he is healthy, enters, and wins seven best-of-five matches, concentrated among a handful of players, with a large downside from injury and age. The rules add a snapshot definition (published ranking at a clock time), a singles-only count and a career-cumulative target that depend on state at issuance.

stages.name: Current standing and the remaining points arithmetic
stages.description: The ranking list at settlement equals current 52-week points minus points dropping off plus points earned in the remaining events. Late in the season both sets are known: drop-offs are deterministic by calendar, and the maximum available points are fixed by the event structure (for example the Finals' round-robin plus knockout allocation). This makes the question closer to a race bounded by arithmetic than to a pure forecast. Finals qualification (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL) uses the same arithmetic on the calendar-year Race, which has no drop-offs: the top eight in the Race after the last counting event qualify (ATP: a current-year major champion ranked 9-20 takes the eighth place, outside knowledge), and because 'qualifies but does not compete' still pays Yes, later withdrawal does not lower the qualifier's probability.
stages.distribution: Deterministic bounds plus a residual uncertainty from match outcomes; the probability of overtaking is zero if the gap exceeds the maximum swing.

stages.name: Event participation and health for remaining events
stages.description: Whether a contender plays the remaining events is a gating variable: withdrawals from the Finals, injuries and fatigue after a long season remove points from the maximum. Injury and age raise the probability that a leader skips events, and a skip can reduce the leader's points to fixed levels.
stages.distribution: Binary participation with strong dependence on injury state; the number of events missed has a heavy tail for injured players.

stages.name: Match-level strength in each remaining event
stages.description: Within events that are played, results depend on surface-adjusted strength; for the year-end rank the surface is mostly indoor hard, so the relevant rating is the indoor-hard rating of the contenders, with a strong dependence on the draw and round-robin groups.
stages.distribution: Match-level Bernoulli draws aggregated through event structure; round-robin events give variance structure that differs from knockout.

stages.name: Major-title probability as a union over four events
stages.description: For the 2027 major contracts, each player has a title probability in each major, depending on the draw, surface, best-of-five edge and health. The probability of at least one title is one minus the product of non-title probabilities, with positive correlation through health and form, so concentrated among the top few players. Variants: a one-season window (KXTENNISMAJORDJOKOVIC, 2025) uses the same union over fewer events; the field contract (KXATPGRANDSLAMFIELD) is one minus the product over remaining majors of P(champion is Alcaraz or Sinner), which needs each named player's participation hazard and the per-event champion distribution of the whole field, so the two players' titles are mutually exclusive within an event and positively linked across events only through health.
stages.distribution: Union of four dependent rare events (individual title probabilities 1-40% for contenders, below 2% for most); strong concentration with heavy skew.

stages.name: Age, longevity and the cumulative-count path
stages.description: A career-cumulative contract needs the player to still be competing and healthy: age-related decline in endurance in best-of-five, injury frequency and retirement hazard all lower the chance of one more major, and the count at issuance fixes the target. For veterans the horizon is short and the probability dominated by availability, not skill.
stages.distribution: Survival-times-conversion structure: P(play a major) times P(win | play); right tail small for players over 38.

stages.name: Snapshot and publication rule
stages.description: The rank contract resolves on the most recently published list at a stated clock time; the publication calendar (rankings are published on Mondays, and in the off-season the list may not change) fixes which list applies. Rules on ties, protected points and withdrawals determine the final figure.
stages.distribution: Calendar-determined discrete rule; error concentrates around ties or last-minute publications.

role_personnel.note: These contracts concern individual players' season totals; there is no lineup or role question. Entry gating is handled under availability and participation inputs.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes act slowly and have no separable effect at the season-aggregate scale; they are absorbed into rating updates and are not observable as a pre-event variable.

environment.note: ten.surface_calendar is WEAK for a November year-end contract; for the 2027 major union each major has a fixed surface and pace (hard, clay, grass, hard) entering through surface-specific ratings and ten.venue_speed_history.

game_context_script.note: No in-match script is relevant to season-end aggregates; round-robin and knockout structure is covered under path simulation and race arithmetic.

officiating_rules.note: No refereeing or officiating factor affects a ranking or major count; the only rules that matter are ranking rules and tie-breaks, treated as settlement.

ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.label: Remaining-points arithmetic to the snapshot date
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.mechanism: Maximum and minimum achievable ranking points by the settlement date for each contender, given drop-offs and remaining events. The same race arithmetic also settles Finals-qualification contracts (cutoff at the 8th place, alternates).
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.rationale: In early November the rank is almost mechanically bounded; probability of overtaking is zero unless the gap is less than the maximum swing, and nonzero only through a small set of events.
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.measurement: For each player compute P_end = P_now - drop(t..T) + sum over remaining events of earned points; maximum earned by event structure (for example Finals: 200 per round-robin win, 400 semifinal, 500 final, 1500 undefeated; Masters 1000 etc.); minimum from not playing; compute the probability of rank 1 (or top 5) by simulation constrained by these bounds; update after each event. As-of: after each Monday publication. Finals qualification (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL; title only): qualifier count is eight singles places, the cutoff is the 8th-place Race to the Finals total at the qualification date, a withdrawn qualifier is replaced by the next alternate in race order, and the probability of qualifying is the simulated probability of finishing in the top eight after applying participation hazards; special exemptions (for example the treatment of Grand Slam winners outside the top eight) and doubles-team qualification are not modelled and are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (sr_finals_qual_contracts).
raw_data: current points, expiry schedule, points table, remaining calendar
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.why: Turns a season-end question into a bounded arithmetic problem with a computable maximum swing, and supplies P(top eight at the cut-off) for KXATPFINALSQUAL/KXWTAFINALSQUAL; per their rules a qualifier who later withdraws still settles Yes, and the ATP Slam-champion exemption must be applied (sr_finals_qual_contracts).

ten.major_participation_hazard.label: Probability of entering each remaining major
ten.major_participation_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters and starts a major) for each of the four majors of 2027, conditional on age, injury state and recent history.
ten.major_participation_hazard.rationale: A major title probability multiplies a participation probability by P(win | play); a veteran or an injured player can have participation well below 1.
ten.major_participation_hazard.measurement: Per player and major, estimate P(start) = 1 - hazard(withdraw before first round), using historical Slam participation by age bin (>=35: lower), injury layoff flag (days since last match>60) and entry list status; logistic with shrinkage n/(n+20). As-of: before each draw.
raw_data: Slam entries and starts by player-year
ten.major_participation_hazard.why: Required to separate availability from skill in a four-event union.

ten.bo5_rating_premium.label: Best-of-five rating premium
ten.bo5_rating_premium.mechanism: Some players outperform their best-of-three rating in best-of-five Slam matches because of endurance or consistency.
ten.bo5_rating_premium.rationale: Men's majors are best-of-five; ratings fitted mainly on best-of-three matches can mis-rank contenders for a major.
ten.bo5_rating_premium.measurement: For each Slam bo5 match, expected win prob E_5 = F(Elo gap) where F is a bo5 transform of the bo3-fitted win prob (via set-win prob s solved from bo3 prob, then bo5 formula). residual_i = sum over player's last up to 60 bo5 matches before as-of with weights 0.5^(age_days/1095) of (result - E_5), divided by the weighted sum of E_5(1-E_5) and by ln10/400 to convert to Elo points, then shrunk by n_eff/(n_eff+25) toward 0. Add the premium to the Elo gap only in best_of=5 matches. As-of: before the event's first match.
raw_data: match rows: best_of, winner/loser ids, date
ten.bo5_rating_premium.why: Corrects ratings for the format used in the major contract, which the catalog treats as a pure format switch.

ten.major_winner_concentration.label: Concentration of recent major winners
ten.major_winner_concentration.mechanism: Share of recent majors won by the top one or two players, a measure of how top-heavy the title distribution is.
ten.major_winner_concentration.rationale: The title probability distribution across players should have a concentration level consistent with history; ratings alone may not reproduce the top-heavy shares.
ten.major_winner_concentration.measurement: Compute the Herfindahl index and top-2 share over the last 12 majors with weights decaying by edition; compare to the model-implied concentration and shrink player probabilities toward the history-implied shares with an initial weight of 0.3 that is a placeholder to be fitted on held-out majors (not calibrated); update after each major. As-of: after each major. It is a calibration check on model-implied concentration, not a driver multiplied into player probabilities.
ten.major_winner_concentration.why: Calibrates the top-heavy title distribution that drives the union probability.

ten.career_major_count_state.label: Career major-count state
ten.career_major_count_state.mechanism: The state variable for cumulative contracts: the player's singles major count and any titles won since the contract was issued.
ten.career_major_count_state.rationale: The 25th-major contract is path-dependent on the count; a title already won shifts the target, and doubles titles are excluded.
ten.career_major_count_state.measurement: Count of singles major titles per player with each date; compare to the contract's target at the as-of date; flag if the count differs from contract assumption. As-of: after each major final.
raw_data: major singles titles with date, tour
ten.career_major_count_state.why: Prevents settlement errors on cumulative contracts when the state changes.

ten.ranking_publication_calendar.label: Ranking publication calendar and snapshot rule
ten.ranking_publication_calendar.mechanism: Which published list applies at the stated settlement clock depends on the publication calendar.
ten.ranking_publication_calendar.rationale: The settlement uses the most recently published list, so a Thursday year-end resolves to the last Monday list; the lists at weeks without events may be identical to the prior one.
ten.ranking_publication_calendar.measurement: Table of publication dates for ATP and WTA by year; for a settlement time T, the applicable list is the latest publication <= T; check history of publications in late December in prior years (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).
raw_data: ranking publication dates and times by week
ten.ranking_publication_calendar.why: Identifies exactly which list will decide the rank contract.

ten.points_defense_rolling.reason: Deterministic drop-offs are the core of rank arithmetic; keep, and pair with the remaining-race calculation.

ten.path_difficulty_sim.reason: A draw-path simulation is a model object, and for the 2027 majors no draw exists yet; its marginal ingredients (surface_rating, rating_uncertainty) are the inputs, so it is context for events with a published draw only.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Base strength; the remaining events are indoor hard so a surface-specific rating matters, and for majors the best-of-five premium adds.

ten.rankings.reason: Current ranks and race points are the same state as the rolling points table; keep the version with expiry dates.

ten.age_career_stage.reason: Drives longevity for cumulative and major contracts; effect is nonlinear.

ten.injury_comeback.reason: Matters for participation but is a flag; participation hazard operationalises it.

ten.pre_draw_field.reason: Entry list and withdrawals before a draw determine participation; relevant only when a draw exists.

ten.surface_calendar.reason: Season transitions matter for early-season rank paths; for a year-end contract in November it has little effect.

m.rules_text.reason: Snapshot time, list name and window definitions are the whole contract.

ten.form.reason: Recent form is mostly in ratings; at season horizon it adds little beyond rating and injury.

ten.motivation.reason: Late-season incentives (year-end #1, qualification for the Finals) affect event choice; weakly measurable.

ten.ranking_points_simulation.reason: A Monte Carlo over the remaining calendar is the model that combines the inputs, not an input; its measurable ingredients are remaining_race_arithmetic, major_participation_hazard, surface_rating and bo5_rating_premium, so it is kept only as the aggregation object.

interactions.mechanism: The probability that a trailing player overtakes the leader is zero if the points gap exceeds the maximum remaining swing, and rises steeply once the gap falls inside it; the effect is a threshold, not a smooth function.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the historical frequency of year-end #1 changes by the ratio of points gap to maximum remaining swing at the start of November.

interactions.mechanism: A veteran's major title probability is the product of a falling participation probability and a falling win probability given participation, so the two age effects compound.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate participation and win conditional separately by age bin and compare the product with the unconditional rate.

interactions.mechanism: The best-of-five premium only applies in majors; a player with high endurance gains most in the later rounds against rivals of similar rating.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress Slam match outcomes on Elo gap with and without the bo5 premium by round.

interactions.mechanism: Concentration makes title probabilities of the top players dependent: when two players dominate, the union probability for the others shrinks together, and the simulation must reproduce the covariance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated top-2 share with historical shares across rolling windows of 12 majors.

interactions.mechanism: If the final points-changing event ends before the last Monday publication, the settlement list is determined; if an event overlaps the snapshot time the arithmetic applies to the previous list only.
interactions.how_to_test: Align historical year-end publications with the final event dates and check which list a Dec 31 12:00 ET snapshot would have used.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold then probit in gap over remaining swing
nonlinearities.why: Rank-1 probability is exactly zero or one outside the feasible swing and varies like a normal CDF of the standardized gap inside it, so the market sensitivity is concentrated near the end of the season.

nonlinearities.shape: accelerating decline in major probability after about 35
nonlinearities.why: Participation, endurance in best-of-five and injury hazard worsen faster than linearly with age, so a linear age effect understates the drop for players above 36.
The probability of at least one title is one minus the product of failures, which saturates for players with moderate per-major probability and compresses differences between contenders.
