contract.settlement_definition: KXATPGSPREAD is a binary on the games differential across the whole match: 'If the game differential in favor of Luca Van Assche across the full match is above 1.5 games', then Yes (strike_type greater, floor_strike 1.5; the title words it as 'win at least 1.5 more games'). The differential is player A's total games minus player B's total games summed over every set including tiebreak sets (the sampled text does not say how a 7-6 tiebreak set or a 10-point match tiebreak/super-tiebreak enters the differential; counting 7-6 as one game for the winner is an assumption); the half-point strike means there is no push. A match that never starts resolves to a fair price; postponed matches stay open for up to two weeks; the retirement clause says that markets that can be unconditionally settled from play already completed settle on it, but the sampled sentence is cut off. The set spread KXATPSSPREAD ('wins by over 1.5 sets', strike_type greater, floor 1.5) is now filed here: Yes only for a 3-0 or 3-1 win in best-of-five (2-0 in best-of-three), driven by ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge; its retirement clause is cut off in the same way.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game differential in favor of Luca Van Assche across the full match is above 1.5 games
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement is the signed games differential for the named player over the full match, strike 1.5, so it is a joint winner-and-margin event, not a winner market.

rules_evidence.quote: If a retirement occurs, all markets that can be unconditionally settled based on play already
rules_evidence.establishes: A retirement only settles rungs that cannot change given play already completed; the remainder of the clause is cut off, so the effect on a spread that is still live is unobserved.

rules_evidence.quote: If Alexander Zverev wins by over 1.5 sets in the Alexander Zverev vs Ben Shelton professional tennis match
rules_evidence.establishes: The set spread is a set-differential handicap at a half-set strike: in best-of-five it is 3-0 or 3-1, in best-of-three only 2-0, so it is a function of the set-count distribution.

variants_and_edge_cases: Title and rule wording differ: the title says 'win at least 1.5 more games' while the rule says 'above 1.5 games'; with a half-point strike they are equivalent, but a whole-number strike (if listed) would need a push rule that is not visible.

Retirement mid-match: the differential at the moment of stopping can be positive for the player who is about to be recorded the loser, so a retiring player who led on games can still be the one whose games differential is above the strike; the sampled clause does not say whether the incomplete match is settled on games played.

Best-of-three versus best-of-five and tiebreak or advantage deciding sets change the number of sets and games over which margin accumulates. An advantage final set (abolished at the majors since 2022, but the format must be checked per event) lengthens the set without widening its margin: once past 6-4 it can only end at a two-game margin (8-6, 12-10), so it adds games, not margin tail; a single set's margin is never above 6.

Two live series with rules sit here (KXATPGSPREAD game differential, KXATPSSPREAD set differential, both ATP men's); no WTA spread series was found, so the WTA treatment (more breaks, smaller margins) is unobserved. A retirement in a set-spread match leaves a 1-0 or 2-0 set lead short of a completed 'win by over 1.5 sets', and the cut-off clause does not say how it settles.
contract.settlement_data_source: Governing-league recorded set scores summed to games per player; the sampled rules text does not name a vendor.

mechanism.summary: The games spread is the signed sum of per-set game margins, so it is a continuous-looking but discrete quantity driven by who holds and who breaks. Per game played the expected margin equals the hold-rate gap, so over the roughly ten games of a tour set it is about ten times the gap (twelve times only over a fixed 12-game window, which overstates the set margin), which means the mean margin depends on the difference of two hold probabilities, while the variance depends on their level and on how often tiebreaks and bagels occur. The winner market is only a coarse projection of this: a match can be won by a player whose games differential is negative (a 7-6 0-6 7-6 pattern) and a favourite who retires still carries the margin accumulated so far. Sets are linked by a latent day-level shock, so margins are heavier-tailed than independent-set models imply, and the match's length is endogenous (a straight-set win stops play early and removes games that would have added margin to either side). The settlement layer adds a mismatch: the contract refers to the full match, while a retirement may truncate the count at the moment the leader or the trailer stops.

stages.name: Hold-rate gap per player
stages.description: The expected games margin per set is proportional to the gap between the two hold probabilities, since each player's wins come from their own service games and from the other player's lost service games. Opponent-adjusted serve and return components give the hold rates for this pair on this court, and the same two numbers also govern the variance of the margin.
stages.distribution: Continuous rates near 0.6-0.9 for tour holds; the margin mean is a linear function of the hold gap (E[games in set] times the gap, about 10 rather than 12 per tour set, see ten.hold_gap_expected_margin) and noise shrinks only slowly with sample size.

stages.name: Per-set margin distribution with tiebreak discreteness
stages.description: Each set ends at 6-0 to 6-4 (margins 6 to 2), 7-5 (2), or 7-6 (1). A tiebreak caps the margin at one game regardless of how dominant the winner was in the tiebreak itself. This creates a probability mass at margin 1 for sets between holders, a mass at 2 for sets with one break, and a thin tail at 5-6 for bagels and breadsticks.
stages.distribution: Discrete support {6,5,4,3,2,1} with heavy mass at 2 and 1 for evenly matched servers; lopsided sets form a separate tail component.

stages.name: Serial dependence between games and sets
stages.description: Games are not independent: a player who has just been broken holds less often and sometimes breaks back; the favourite serving to stay in a set is under different pressure than a game at 2-2. At the set level the day-level form shock links sets. Together they thicken the tails of the margin relative to an independent model.
stages.distribution: Positive serial correlation in game results within a set (small, around 0.05-0.1) and between sets (larger); heavier tails than a sum of independent binomials.

stages.name: Endogenous match length and format
stages.description: The number of sets played depends on the outcomes: a 6-3 6-2 win ends play at two sets, whereas a 6-3 3-6 6-2 win accumulates a third set whose margin may be positive or negative. Best-of-five gives more sets for margin to compound. Because games are only counted while play continues, margin variance and mean are functions of match length that is itself chosen by the outcomes. The set spread KXATPSSPREAD ('wins by over 1.5 sets') is read directly off this stage: it is the named player's straight-set or one-set-dropped win in best-of-five (3-0, 3-1), i.e. P(win) times P(at most one set lost | win) from ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge, which is why the set-count input sits here.
stages.distribution: Mixture over set counts; the straight-set branch has margin concentrated near +5 to +8 for the winner, the decider branch has margin near 0 to +3.

stages.name: Tour, gender and level differences
stages.description: WTA matches have more breaks, so the same rating gap converts into a smaller expected games margin and a different distribution of 3-set outcomes; Challenger and ITF levels have a larger spread of player quality and more dispersion in margin. A model fit on ATP tour data will mis-size women's or lower-level spreads.
stages.distribution: Tour-level shifts in the average hold probability (for example about 0.80 for ATP vs 0.65 for WTA) and in the dispersion of margin.

stages.name: Retirement truncation of the margin
stages.description: If a player retires, the games differential stops accumulating at the moment of retirement. The retiring player is usually trailing, so the truncated margin is typically positive for the opponent and often well below a full-match margin; the rung that settles depends on the truncated clause.
stages.distribution: Rare truncation event, concentrated in the trailing player; the margin at retirement is usually 2-6 games in the opponent's favour.

role_personnel.note: A singles game spread involves two fixed players and no lineup or role; participation changes void to a fair price before play and are not a role variable.

coaching_scheme.note: Tactical and coaching adjustments have no pre-match observable at the margin level; their effect appears indirectly in serial dependence between sets.

environment.note: Court speed, altitude, indoor state and ball condition shift the hold level, hence tiebreak mass and margin variance; ten.venue_speed_history (event hold and ace history from match data) is the available proxy and ten.court_cond the condition flags, both shared with the totals and set records. A verified public per-event pace index is still missing (sp_court_pace).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Recent minutes, sets and five-set exposure (ten.workload_minutes) define fatigue concretely; ten.fatigue is WEAK for the margin on its own so the defined load quantity is attached.

ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.label: Hold-gap implied expected games margin
ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.mechanism: Expected games differential over a full 12-game window is 12 times the difference of the two hold probabilities, a quantity with its own measurement noise.
ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.rationale: The model reduces to a simple relationship between hold gap and margin that is easy to estimate and check; the catalog has hold and break but not the margin as a first-class variable.
ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.measurement: Opponent-adjusted spw for each player from matches strictly before the match day (12-month half-life, same method as ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return); hold h via closed-form game formula h(spw). For each set run the DP over game scores with alternating serve (average over first server) to get the set margin pmf, E[D_set], Var; roll over sets using the set-count distribution for the format. Report mean and SD of total game margin with spw drawn from Beta posterior (SD about 0.015). Do not use E[N]*(hA-hB) except as a check.
free_sources: Sackmann CSV w_svpt, w_1stWon, w_2ndWon, l_ columns
ten.hold_gap_expected_margin.why: Connects the hold model directly to the spread strike so mean and strike can be compared with the right variance.

ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.label: Calibrated game-margin probability mass function
ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.mechanism: The empirical distribution of match games differential by pre-match edge, format and tour, with tiebreak-induced discreteness.
ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.rationale: Smooth normal approximations miss the 1-game masses created by tiebreaks and the 5-6 game tails created by bagels; a calibrated PMF corrects both and is not a market price.
ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.measurement: For each historical completed match (retirements/walkovers excluded) record D = games won by the winner minus loser signed from player A's view, with pre-match Elo-implied p_A computed from ratings updated only through the prior day. Bin p_A in 5-point bins by tour x best_of x surface; empirical pmf per bin smoothed with a Gaussian kernel over adjacent bins (bandwidth 1 bin); shrink to a discretised-normal fit of D on logit(p_A) with weight n/(n+50). Output P(D>k) for half-integer k. Walk-forward only.
ten.game_margin_pmf_calibration.why: Gives the exact discrete tail probabilities that a Gaussian approximation mis-sizes at half-point strikes.

ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.label: Margin given win conversion curve
ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.mechanism: The probability that a match winner also has a games margin above a threshold, as a function of pair edge and format.
ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.rationale: Spread settlement mixes winner and margin; the share of wins that are close (negative or small margins) rises as the gap shrinks and in best-of-five, and matters more than the mean margin at the strike.
ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.measurement: From Sackmann scores compute for each edge bin P(D>k | winner) and P(D<0 | winner) by format; fit a logistic in edge and format; shrink to pooled values with n/(n+60). Combine with the winner probability: P(D>1.5)=P(win)*P(D>1.5|win)+P(lose)*P(D>1.5|lose). The edge bins use the market-free P(win) from the match_winner model (surface- and pace-adjusted Elo variant, stated in the dataset), never a price-implied probability.
ten.win_margin_conversion_curve.why: Prevents treating the games spread as a shifted winner probability when a sizeable share of wins are close.

ten.game_serial_dependence.label: Serial dependence of game results within and across sets
ten.game_serial_dependence.mechanism: The chance a player holds depends on whether he was just broken and on set-state pressure.
ten.game_serial_dependence.rationale: Independent game results understate the clustering of breaks; the thickness of the margin tail relies on this serial effect.
ten.game_serial_dependence.measurement: From Slam point-by-point build one row per service game: hold (0/1), server id, returner id, prior_game_broken (previous game was a break against this server), serving_to_stay (opponent leads by one game and a further loss loses the set), set index, surface. Logit(hold) ~ server effect + returner effect + prior_game_broken + serving_to_stay with server random slope on prior_game_broken; report pooled coefficient with CI and per-player slope shrunk n/(n+60). Use matches before as-of only.
raw_data: game-by-game winner and server within sets
ten.game_serial_dependence.why: Provides the explicit within-set clustering that underlies heavy margin tails.

ten.retirement_margin_state.label: Games margin at retirement
ten.retirement_margin_state.mechanism: If the match is truncated by retirement, the games differential at that moment determines whether the spread rung can be settled.
ten.retirement_margin_state.rationale: The margin at retirement is usually favourable to the non-retiring player and is smaller than a typical completed-match margin; the spread settlement depends on it.
ten.retirement_margin_state.measurement: From Sackmann score strings with RET, extract games for each player at retirement; estimate the distribution of D at retirement by tour and by which player retired; shrink pooled with n/(n+30). Report P(D>1.5 | retirement).
ten.retirement_margin_state.why: Quantifies the retirement tail for a spread contract whose retirement clause is cut off in the sample.

ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.label: Set-count distribution by edge and format
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.mechanism: The probability mass over 2/3 sets (bo3) or 3/4/5 sets (bo5) as a function of pair edge, surface and tour.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.rationale: Total sets and set spread contracts are direct functions of this distribution; 'any set' is its straight-set complement. The existing catalog lists match length in games but not the set-count distribution.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.measurement: For each completed match (retirements excluded) compute pre-match Elo win prob p from ratings through the prior day. Bin p in 5-point bins by tour x best_of x surface; empirical P(N sets) per bin, fitted by a monotone logistic in logit(p); shrink bin value toward the fit with weight n/(n+40) (no separate additive shrink). Output P(decider), P(straight sets), P(winner dropped a set) per format, walk-forward only.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.why: Shared definition with set_winner_and_any_set (single definition of the set-count and straight-set mass); supplies the set-differential rungs of KXATPSSPREAD (3-0/3-1 in best-of-five, 2-0 in best-of-three) that this archetype owns by target.

ten.hold_break.reason: The engine of the game margin; best as an explicit hold gap, not as a Markov chain that hides uncertainty.

ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return.reason: Pair-specific serve and return rates determine each player's hold; the correct basis for the margin.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Elo gap maps to margin only loosely (linear in the middle, flat at the extremes); better to map through hold rates than from the rating directly.

ten.lopsided_set_rate.reason: Captures the bagel and breadstick tail but overlaps the PMF; useful as player-specific dispersion.

ten.within_match_dependence.reason: Widens the margin distribution relative to independence and affects the tails most; hard to estimate.

ten.format.reason: Number of sets and the final-set rule change both the mean and the tail of the margin; coded exactly.

ten.tour_gender_effect.reason: Real, since WTA hold levels differ, but best expressed through hold levels rather than a tour dummy.

ten.retirement_base_rate.reason: Sizes the truncation frequency, but without timing and margin state it cannot say how many rungs are affected.

ten.retirement_settlement_rules.reason: The retirement clause is cut off in the sample, so its content decides the tail; primary because unresolved.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Its catalog measurement fits a distribution to Kalshi mid prices across rungs and reports an implied PMF, so it is market-derived: useful only to benchmark and sanity-check model rung probabilities (monotonicity, sum-to-one), never as an outcome input or a coverage claim.

ten.second_serve_vulnerability.reason: Second-serve points are where most breaks occur, so it is informative for hold, but it overlaps adjusted serve and return.

ten.surface_similarity.reason: Stabilises estimates for thin surfaces; a pooling device, not a driver.

ten.fatigue.reason: Late-set fade effects on margin are small and poorly measured; mostly noise relative to the hold gap.

interactions.mechanism: The expected margin scales with the number of games played, so the same hold gap produces a mean margin about 1.6 times larger in best-of-five than in best-of-three, but the straight-set stopping rule limits the increase.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the realised mean D per hold gap bin for bo3 and bo5 and test the ratio against the expected 5/3 games ratio adjusted for set counts.

interactions.mechanism: Bagels and breadsticks concentrate in matches with a large rating gap, so the tail of margin grows faster than the mean as the gap increases; a player-level lopsided rate adds to this for the favourite.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot P(D>=8) against rating gap bins split by the favourite's lopsided-set rate.

interactions.mechanism: With low hold levels (WTA) both players break often, so the margin variance is high but its mean depends on return strength more than on serve; with high holds (ATP) tiebreaks cap the margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate separate margin-vs-hold-gap slopes for ATP and WTA and test equality.

interactions.mechanism: In retirement matches the margin is truncated: either the contract settles on games played (favouring the leader's cover) or leaves the market for the unconditional clause, flipping which side of the strike a late-leading favourite lands on.
interactions.how_to_test: For historical retirements, compute D at stoppage and compare cover outcomes under both settlement rules.

interactions.mechanism: Both inputs create positive dependence at different scales (games within a set and sets within a match); together they determine the covariance of games across the match and the variance of D.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a model with only one dependence layer and one with both, comparing the calibration of P(|D|>6).

nonlinearities.why: The mean margin is linear in the hold gap but the variance falls as hold levels increase because tiebreak sets cap the margin at 1; the strike probability is therefore not linear in the gap.
A small increase in a player's bagel rate increases P(D>=8) disproportionately because margins of 6 and 5 in one set stack with another lopsided set.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating mapping from rating gap to expected margin
nonlinearities.why: Rating gap converts to games margin roughly linearly in the middle but flattens for very large gaps because the loser still wins about two games per set.

contract.settlement_definition: After the reconciliation one series is filed here: KXATPTIEBREAK ('Tiebreak to occur in Match'), title only with no rules text recovered. A tiebreak-occurs contract would settle Yes if at least one set of the named match reaches a tiebreak; whether a deciding-set 10-point tiebreak counts, how a retirement before any tiebreak is treated, and the source are not visible. The tournament sweep series KXATPSETSWEEP has moved to tournament_winner_futures. Sibling match series that do have rules (totals, spreads, set winners) settle a match that never starts at a fair price and on retirement settle only markets decided by completed play; applying that to KXATPTIEBREAK is an inference.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tiebreak scope: does the contract count a deciding-set 10-point match tiebreak or only the 7-point tiebreak after a 6-6 set; does a tiebreak in a retired match that already happened settle Yes at once (an early settlement the clause for 'unconditionally settled' markets would allow).
Format dependence: a best-of-five gives five chances for a tiebreak and four sets that can be dropped, while WTA best-of-three gives half as many exposures.

Retirement: a tiebreak that already occurred locks Yes under the sibling series' 'unconditionally settled' clause; with no tiebreak yet, the unsettled side depends on the cut-off remainder of that clause (inferred, no KXATPTIEBREAK text).
Straight-set matches cap exposure: a 2-0 or 3-0 match offers the minimum number of sets for a tiebreak, so the favourite's sweep probability enters this contract only as a suppressor of exposure.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated; presumably governing-league recorded set scores with the tiebreak marked in the score string.

mechanism.summary: A tiebreak occurs in a set when it reaches six-all, i.e. each player wins six of the first twelve games without either leading by two at 6-x; ten holds is the modal path but alternating breaks also get there. Its probability is a very steep, convex function of the two hold probabilities: at equal holds of 0.80 about 22% of sets reach 6-6, at 0.90 about 38%. A match-level event is then the union over the sets that are played, and the number of sets itself rises with closeness, which is also what produces tiebreaks, so the events are positively dependent across sets and with match length. Because the hold probabilities on the day are uncertain, the convexity means the expected tiebreak probability exceeds the tiebreak probability computed at the expected hold. Straight-set matches are the main suppressor of exposure: the favourite sweeping removes the sets in which a tiebreak could occur, which happens when the edge is large and the sets are positively correlated through a day-level form shock. A retirement and format layer sits on top: a tiebreak that has already occurred locks the contract.

stages.name: Serve hold levels for both players
stages.description: Everything starts with how often each player holds serve against the other. A tiebreak requires the set to reach 6-6, which happens whenever each player wins six of the first twelve games without leading by two earlier; ten holds is the modal path but four or more alternating breaks also reach 6-6, while a hold gap produces straight-set matches with fewer sets; the same two hold probabilities therefore act on the tiebreak event twice, through the per-set 6-6 chance and through the number of sets.
stages.distribution: Two rates in the 0.6-0.92 range; the sum of holds drives tiebreak odds and the difference drives sweep odds.

stages.name: Per-set probability of reaching six-all
stages.description: With holds computed, the probability of 6-6 follows from a dynamic program over the games of the set. It is strongly convex in hold: 0.18 at 0.75, 0.22 at 0.80, 0.28 at 0.85, 0.38 at 0.90. Uncertainty about the day's hold level therefore increases expected tiebreak mass relative to the point estimate.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per set with probability rising steeply and convexly with hold level; Jensen gap of about two to three points of probability from hold uncertainty.

stages.name: Exposure across sets and format
stages.description: The match-level tiebreak event is a union across the sets played, so the number of sets is an exposure variable: more sets means more chances. Best-of-five and close matches both raise exposure; a deciding set that uses a tiebreak at 6-6 adds an extra exposure with its own rule.
stages.distribution: Union of dependent Bernoulli events across 2-5 sets; exposure itself is random and positively correlated with the event.

stages.name: Dependence across sets and clustering of serving form
stages.description: A player with a hot serving day holds throughout, making tiebreaks in consecutive sets more likely together; the same shock widens the gap and shortens the match. The dependence means the probability of at least one tiebreak is below the independent union but the probability of two or more is above the independent product.
stages.distribution: Positive correlation between sets; overdispersed tiebreak counts relative to a Binomial with a constant p.

stages.name: Straight-set matches as the suppressor of tiebreak exposure
stages.description: The number of sets in which a tiebreak can occur is two or three in best-of-three and three to five in best-of-five, and the minimum is reached when the favourite wins in straight sets. A heavy favourite therefore lowers the match-level tiebreak probability twice: through a lower per-set 6-6 probability and through fewer sets. The straight-set probability depends on the edge, on player-specific set-drop tendencies beyond rating and on whether a tiebreak lottery intervenes, which makes the set-count and tiebreak events jointly determined rather than separable.
stages.distribution: Set count is a discrete mixture (2/3 or 3/4/5) whose straight-set mass rises steeply with edge; the joint tiebreak/set-count table is non-separable.

stages.name: Truncation and settlement
stages.description: A retirement ends the match: a tiebreak already played settles the occurs-contract Yes early under the sibling series' unconditional-settlement clause, while a retirement before any tiebreak leaves the No side to the unseen remainder of that clause. Truncation is small in probability but one-sided: it can only remove future tiebreak exposure, and it is more likely for players with a pre-match physical problem. KXATPTIEBREAK's own text is not available.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event; it can only remove future tiebreak exposure, so for the occurs contract it is one-sided (an already-played tiebreak locks Yes).

ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.label: Hold-rate uncertainty propagation (Jensen correction)
ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.mechanism: Because P(6-6) is convex in hold, uncertainty about hold raises expected tiebreak probability.
ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.rationale: Plugging point-estimate holds into the tiebreak formula understates the probability by a few points: averaging 0.80 and 0.90 gives 0.30 while the probability at the mean hold 0.85 is 0.28.
ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.measurement: Matchup spw_A and spw_B from opponent-adjusted components (ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return). Beta posterior: mean = adjusted spw, effective n = sum of 0.5^(age_days/365) over serve points in the last 24 months (cap 4000). Draw 2000 pairs, add day shock N(0,0.02^2) on spw, convert to holds with the closed-form game formula, compute P(6-6) by set DP per draw, return E[p66] and E[p66]-p66(mean h). As-of: data through the day before.
raw_data: serve points won and played per player-surface with dates
ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation.why: Corrects a systematic bias in a convex event's probability that no existing input addresses.

ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.label: Tiebreak and sweep base rates by event and format
ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.mechanism: Empirical frequency of at least one tiebreak per match, and of straight-set wins, by tournament-edition and format.
ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.rationale: Event-level conditions (indoor courts, altitude) produce persistent tiebreak rates that exceed what player stats imply; the base rate is a prior to be updated by the pair.
ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.measurement: For each tournament, compute the share of matches with at least one tiebreak and the share won without dropping a set over the last three editions, weighted with half-life 18 months and shrunk to the tour-level rate with n/(n+60); provide split by round and best_of. As-of: before the event.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings (tiebreak shown in parentheses)
raw_data: score strings by tournament, year, round
ten.tiebreak_base_rate_by_event.why: Provides the event-specific prior that player-based estimates miss.

ten.player_set_drop_propensity.label: Player set-drop propensity beyond rating
ten.player_set_drop_propensity.mechanism: Some players win more matches in straight sets than their rating implies, others drop sets habitually.
ten.player_set_drop_propensity.rationale: The sweep probability depends on the pattern of set loss, not only on win probability; style and consistency produce heterogeneity.
ten.player_set_drop_propensity.measurement: Per player, residual = share of wins in straight sets minus the model expectation given opponent rating; average over the last 60 wins with half-life 12 months and shrink to 0 with n/(n+25); test split-sample persistence before use; include format and round.
ten.player_set_drop_propensity.why: Captures style-specific sweep tendencies that Elo alone does not provide.

ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.label: Joint table of tiebreak occurrence and straight-set win
ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.mechanism: Tiebreak occurrence and sweeps are not independent because big-serving pairs produce many 7-6 7-6 straight-set wins.
ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.rationale: If the two contracts are listed together, their dependence is relevant for combined pricing and for checking that marginals are consistent.
ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.measurement: For each historical match compute pre-match hold probabilities h_A,h_B from opponent-adjusted serve stats through the prior day. Bin by mean hold (0.05 wide) x |hold gap| (0.05 wide) x best_of. Build the 2x2 table counts (any tiebreak, winner won without losing a set); smooth with add-0.5 Laplace; shrink cell probabilities to the product of marginals with weight n/(n+80); report odds ratio per bin with CI. Retirements excluded.
ten.tiebreak_sweep_joint_table.why: Quantifies the dependence between the two event types for correct joint and consistency checks.

ten.tournament_set_drop_path.label: Tournament-level set-drop path probabilities
ten.tournament_set_drop_path.mechanism: The probability that a player wins a whole tournament without dropping a set is a product across rounds of per-match straight-set probabilities.
ten.tournament_set_drop_path.rationale: If KXATPSETSWEEP means a tournament-level sweep (title unclear), the contract is a path product with the seven or more match-level straight-set probabilities, and correlated with the title probability itself.
ten.tournament_set_drop_path.measurement: Run the bracket simulation (ten.path_difficulty_sim) with per-match P(win, straight sets) from ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge. P(title without dropping a set) = share of sims where the player wins all rounds, each in straight sets. Correlation: add a player-level latent form shock z~N(0,s^2) to the Elo gap shared across rounds with s estimated by matching the historical share of title runs without a set lost for top-8 seeds; report P with and without the shock. As-of: draw publication.
raw_data: draw, results by round for past events
ten.tournament_set_drop_path.why: Not used by KXATPTIEBREAK; kept only as this record's original definition. KXATPSETSWEEP (tournament-level sweep) now sits in tournament_winner_futures, whose stage s7 uses this input.

ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.mechanism: The probability mass over 2/3 sets (bo3) or 3/4/5 sets (bo5) as a function of pair edge, surface and tour.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.rationale: Total sets and set spread contracts are direct functions of this distribution; 'any set' is its straight-set complement. The existing catalog lists match length in games but not the set-count distribution.

Bin p in 5-point bins by tour x best_of x surface; empirical P(N sets) per bin, fitted by a monotone logistic in logit(p); shrink bin value toward the fit with weight n/(n+40) (no separate additive shrink). Output P(decider), P(straight sets), P(winner dropped a set) per format, walk-forward only.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.why: Supplies P(straight sets) by edge and format, which caps the number of sets in which a tiebreak can occur (stage s5).

ten.venue_speed_history.reason: Event pace shifts both holds at once, producing persistent event-level tiebreak rates.

ten.within_match_dependence.reason: Governs clustering across sets and the dependence of sweeps; hard to estimate.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Sweep probability depends on the rating gap, tiebreak on both holds; a secondary input for the tiebreak contract.

ten.retirement_settlement_rules.reason: No rules text is available at all; the treatment of retirement and unplayed sets is the main contract risk.

ten.tiebreak.reason: Tiebreak win rate does not affect whether a tiebreak occurs, only who wins it; irrelevant to the occurs contract and weak for sweeps.

ten.serve_return.reason: Raw serve and return rates are the ingredients of hold probabilities; keep the hold definition.

interactions.mechanism: A shared day-level shock makes straight-set wins for the favourite more likely and also makes tiebreak counts overdispersed, so the same parameter shifts both tails.

interactions.mechanism: Style-specific sweep tendencies saturate with the favourite's edge: they add little for a heavy favourite and matter in the middle of the edge distribution.

nonlinearities.shape: convex rise with hold level (0.18 at 0.75, 0.38 at 0.90)
nonlinearities.why: Reaching 6-6 requires twelve games of mostly holds, so the probability rises faster than linearly with hold; small errors in hold at the top of the range produce large errors in probability.
Match-level tiebreak probability is one minus the product of set non-tiebreak probabilities, so extra sets add less than linearly with positive dependence and exposure saturates for high p.
Straight-set probability is near 25% for even pairs in best-of-three and rises toward the favourite's win probability for large gaps; the middle range is steepest.

contract.settlement_definition: Two settled families sit here after the reconciliation. Set winner (KXATPSETWINNER and KXWTASETWINNER, both with recovered rules): 'If Arthur Nagel wins set 2 ... then the market resolves to Yes' and 'If Janice Tjen wins set 2 in the Janice Tjen vs Magda Linette professional tennis match', a binary on one named player taking one named set, a different object from the match winner. Any set (KXATPANYSET, title only): presumably Yes if the named player wins at least one set, i.e. one minus the opponent's straight-sets probability. Non-occurrence before the first ball resolves to fair price and postponement stays open two weeks; the retirement clause ('all markets that can be unconditionally settled based on play already completed wi...') is cut off, so an unplayed or interrupted named set is not defined.

rules_evidence.quote: If Arthur Nagel wins set 2 in the Jacob Fearnley vs Arthur Nagel professional tennis match
rules_evidence.establishes: The named player must win the named set; a set number is part of the strike, not a match or a game.

rules_evidence.quote: If Janice Tjen wins set 2 in the Janice Tjen vs Magda Linette professional tennis match
rules_evidence.establishes: The WTA set winner contract has the same wording as the ATP one, so best-of-three (set 2 always played unless the match ends early by retirement) applies.

variants_and_edge_cases: Set that may not be played: 'set 3' in a best-of-three exists only if the match is 1-1, so a set-3 winner contract is conditional on a decider; the sampled text does not say whether an unplayed set resolves No or to a fair price (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).

Any-set wording: KXATPANYSET is title-only, so whether 'any set' means the named player wins at least one set, or any set reaches a named state, and how a retirement before the player wins a set is treated, are not visible.

Series set: KXATPSETWINNER and KXWTASETWINNER (rules text, named set number) and KXATPANYSET (title only); the WTA sample names set 2 of a best-of-three final, which is always played unless the match ends by retirement in set 1.
contract.settlement_data_source: Governing-league recorded set scores; vendor not named in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: A set is a race to six games with a two-game margin and a tiebreak at six-all, so a set-level win probability is generated by the two hold probabilities and by the first server. Set markets differ from match markets because a set has fewer points and a larger share of noise: the first-set win probability of a 75% match favourite is much closer to 50%. The set-winner and any-set contracts are transforms of the same sequence of set outcomes: a named set is a marginal over the other sets and 'any set' is one minus the opponent's straight-sets probability (total sets and set spread, now in sibling archetypes, are further transforms of the same sequence). Both depend on how the outcome of one set shifts the next, which is where momentum, a day-level form shock, fatigue and tactical adjustment sit, and where the conditional probability that a set exists (a third set only if 1-1) becomes part of the price. Two further layers sit outside the point model: the possibility that a set is interrupted by a retirement, and the ambiguity about an unplayed set.

stages.name: Set existence and format
stages.description: The first question is whether the named set will be played at all. A third set in best-of-three exists only after 1-1; a fifth set in best-of-five only after 2-2; the existence indicator is exactly what the set-count distribution supplies. Format therefore turns a named later-set winner into a conditional contract, and KXATPANYSET into one minus the opponent's straight-sets mass.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli existence indicators with a cascade structure; the probability of reaching set 5 is a product of three set outcomes.

stages.name: Set-one probability with first-server adjustment
stages.description: Set 1 is the baseline: the pair's hold and break rates give P(A wins set 1), shaded by who serves first and by the chance of a tiebreak. First-set probabilities are noisier than match probabilities, so favourites are shaded toward 0.5 and the shading is larger on fast courts and for big servers.
stages.distribution: Binomial-like around 0.45-0.70; the tiebreak at 6-6 is close to a coin flip adding variance on fast courts.

stages.name: Set-index calibration
stages.description: Win probabilities differ by set number, not only by prior result: the first set carries the settling-in effect (pace of the court, nerves) and the final set carries physical cost and the tiebreak rule. The same pair edge therefore produces a different set-win probability in set 1, set 2 and a decider.
stages.distribution: Systematic shift by set index (illustratively 1-4 points of win probability; unsourced and to be estimated, not assumed); larger for older players and long events.

stages.name: Dependence between consecutive sets
stages.description: Conditional on losing set 1, the probability of winning set 2 falls but usually remains above the base for a favourite; conditional on winning, it rises. Part of this is latent day-level form; part is momentum and tactical change; part is the loser's injury. The size of the link determines the whole spread of the set-count distribution.
stages.distribution: Positive correlation between adjacent set outcomes after controlling for edge (an assumed 0.1-0.3 is unsourced and not identified from set scores alone, see es_dependence_estimation); heavier for bo5.

stages.name: Aggregation to named-set and any-set outcomes
stages.description: The sequence of set results is then summed to the quantities settled: the named set's winner, or at least one set won (any set). These are path-counting transforms: 'any set' is one minus the opponent's straight-sets probability, and a named later set needs the path that makes it exist.
stages.distribution: Discrete distributions over 2-3 (bo3) or 3-5 (bo5) sets; tail probabilities such as 5 sets are sensitive to dependence.

stages.name: Interruption and unplayed-set handling
stages.description: A retirement or walkover can end the match during a set, leaving an unplayed or unfinished set; the settlement outcome of the named set or the any-set contract then depends on the unobserved clause. Pre-match signals of a physical problem precede most such interruptions.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event with timing concentrated in the first two sets; heavier tail in bo5.

role_personnel.note: A set contract involves the two fixed players of one match; there is no lineup, rotation or role question that a pre-match variable could address.

coaching_scheme.note: Between-set tactical adjustments are real but unobserved before the match; the aggregate is the set-to-set dependence estimated from historical sequences, which is not a coaching input.

environment.note: Court pace, ball, indoor state and wind move hold level and tiebreak incidence and thus the set score and set-count mass; the inputs are the same ones used in the totals, aces and spreads records, with a verified public pace index still missing (sw_env_gap).

ten.set_number_calibration.label: Set-index and previous-set calibration offsets
ten.set_number_calibration.mechanism: Win probability for a given edge differs by set number and by the previous set's result.
ten.set_number_calibration.rationale: The match model implies a single set-win probability but empirical frequencies show set-index effects (first set cautious, deciders fatigue and tiebreak formats). A naive model that reuses one probability across sets misprices set-3 and set-5 contracts.
ten.set_number_calibration.measurement: From Sackmann score strings compute, for the favourite by edge bin, the empirical win frequency in set 1, set 2 given won/lost 1, set 3 given 1-1, bo5 set 4 and set 5 conditional on state; fit a logistic with edge, set index and prior-set result dummies, shrink toward the pooled model with n/(n+50). Output offsets in logit units per set index and state. Interpretation limit: score strings give only the net conditional offset by set index and prior-set result (latent day form, momentum and fatigue combined); separating latent form from momentum needs point-level data that exist for Slams only, as exact_set_score's es_dependence_estimation states.
ten.set_number_calibration.why: Prices a specific named set rather than assuming all sets share the match-level probability.

ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.label: Set-count distribution by edge and format
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.mechanism: The probability mass over 2/3 sets (bo3) or 3/4/5 sets (bo5) as a function of pair edge, surface and tour.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.rationale: Total sets and set spread contracts are direct functions of this distribution; 'any set' is its straight-set complement. The existing catalog lists match length in games but not the set-count distribution.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.measurement: For each completed match (retirements excluded) compute pre-match Elo win prob p from ratings through the prior day. Bin p in 5-point bins by tour x best_of x surface; empirical P(N sets) per bin, fitted by a monotone logistic in logit(p); shrink bin value toward the fit with weight n/(n+40) (no separate additive shrink). Output P(decider), P(straight sets), P(winner dropped a set) per format, walk-forward only.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.why: Gives the empirical backbone for total sets, set spread and any-set contracts that overlap in one set-count distribution.

ten.within_match_serve_decay.label: Within-match serve and movement decay profile
ten.within_match_serve_decay.mechanism: A player's serve-point win rate drifts down in later sets, and the drift differs by age, previous workload and match length.
ten.within_match_serve_decay.rationale: Late-set contracts (set 4, set 5, set 3 of a bo3) depend on fatigue effects that appear within the match rather than in rest days; a pre-match fatigue number only partly predicts it.
ten.within_match_serve_decay.measurement: From Slam point-by-point compute spw_set_k per player in bo5 matches lasting >=3 sets; decay_k = spw_{k+1} - spw_k per player-match. Pooled mixed model decay ~ set_index + age>=33 + prior_match_minutes>200 + heat_flag + (1|player); player estimate = pooled prediction + player random effect shrunk n/(n+25) toward 0. Use only matches before as-of; report expected spw change by set index.
raw_data: point-level server and winner by set
ten.within_match_serve_decay.why: Provides the within-match mechanism that distinguishes deciding sets and set 4/5 contracts from set 1.

ten.hold_break.reason: Generates set-level win probabilities and tiebreak chances; essential but model-level, so its uncertainty must be propagated.

ten.opp_adjusted_serve_return.reason: Pair-specific serve and return rates are the base of every set contract; the right primary role.

ten.within_match_dependence.reason: Controls the set-count distribution and the any-set and sweep tail; weakly identified, so calibration is critical.

ten.first_serve_in_variance.reason: Day-to-day first-serve percentage variance moves set outcomes together; measurable only post hoc, so use as variance parameter, not predictor.

ten.tiebreak_reach_probability.reason: Useful for set score and total-sets paths through decider formats; derived from hold probabilities.

ten.decider_record.reason: Small samples; first-set conversion is better pooled than by player.

ten.fatigue.reason: Pre-match fatigue has a small effect on set 1 and larger on later sets; defined by recent minutes and rest.

ten.retirement_settlement_rules.reason: The retirement clause is cut off and an unplayed set is not defined; both are settlement-critical.

ten.market_odds.reason: A bookmaker match price is not an input to set outcomes; it can serve as a consistency benchmark only.

ten.break_points.reason: Break-point statistics are outcomes of the same point process; adds no information beyond the hold rates.

ten.tiebreak.reason: Tiebreak records are noisy and regress to serve strength; only matters for decider formats.

ten.withdrawal_signals.reason: Practice and press signals precede interruptions, which affect whether a set is completed; timestamp vintage is important.

ten.match_length_expectation.reason: Expected service games per set sets tiebreak incidence; redundant with the hold chain but a convenient summary.

interactions.mechanism: The set-index offset differs between best-of-three and best-of-five because the later sets of a bo5 occur after much longer play; a set-3 contract in bo3 faces a different offset than set 3 of a bo5.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate set-index offsets separately by format on historical matches and compare.

interactions.mechanism: The dependence parameter reshapes the entire set-count distribution: higher correlation raises straight-set and fifth-set mass together at the expense of 3-1 or 2-1 outcomes.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with varying correlations and compare marginal P(5 sets) and P(straight sets) with historical frequencies by edge.

interactions.mechanism: In-match serve decay becomes important only after long previous matches, with older players above a workload threshold showing a clear drop in set 4-5 spw.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress set-5 spw change on previous-match minutes with a threshold at about 200 minutes.

interactions.mechanism: Tiebreaks are most likely in sets between big servers, and first-serve percentage variance makes the six-all branch more frequent for the player who has a good serving day.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare tiebreak frequency in sets where first-serve percentage exceeded the player's average by more than 5 points.

interactions.mechanism: A serve decay across sets lowers hold late in a long match, so the set-index offset in the decider is larger for players with a measured spw drop than for steady servers; the offset is therefore conditional on the serve-decay regime, mostly in best-of-five matches that reach set four or five.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the set-index offset separately for player-matches with a negative versus non-negative within-match spw slope and test the difference in set 4 and 5 win rates controlling for edge.

nonlinearities.shape: convex effect on tail of set counts
nonlinearities.why: Small increases in the between-set correlation have a larger effect on P(5 sets) and P(straight sets) than on the mean number of sets, because the tails scale with the covariance.
Tiebreak incidence per set rises faster than linearly as both hold probabilities rise above 0.8 because six-all requires holds through twelve games.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped in edge for straight sets
nonlinearities.why: P(straight-sets win) rises slowly for even matches, steeply for moderate favourites, then saturates near the favourite's match win probability.

contract.settlement_definition: The three live games-total series settle on a single number: 'If the number of completed games in the full match is above 28.5 ... then the market resolves to Yes' (strike_type greater, floor_strike at a half point, so no push). The count is every completed game in every set of the match, where counting a tiebreak as one game (a 7-6 set contributing 13) and counting a deciding set's own games are conventions not stated in the sampled text, and an interrupted game at retirement is read as not 'completed' only because the rule says 'completed games'. Non-occurrence before the first ball resolves to a fair price, postponements stay open up to two weeks, and the retirement sentence in the sample says only that markets that can be unconditionally settled from completed play settle on it (cut off). Total sets (KXATPTOTALSETS, now filed here): 'If above 4.5 sets are played' (strike greater, floor 4.5), so in best-of-five it is the five-set event and the bo3 analogue would be 2.5; a fifth set begun and then cut by retirement is presumably 'played' but this is not stated. Whether a 10-point match tiebreak that replaces a third set counts as one game or ten points is not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If the number of completed games in the full match is above 32.5 in the Carlos Alcaraz vs Casper Ruud professional tennis match
rules_evidence.establishes: The settled quantity is the count of completed games over the full match against a half-point strike; no push is possible.

rules_evidence.establishes: The WTA series uses the same wording as the ATP ones, so the structure is identical but the level of the strike (26.5 versus 28.5 or 32.5) reflects tour and format.

variants_and_edge_cases: Retirement asymmetry: the 'over' side can be settled Yes if the completed games already exceed the strike when a player retires, whereas the 'under' side cannot be settled until the match completes; a retirement therefore favours rungs that were already crossed (the retirement sentence in the sample is cut off, so this is inferred).

Assumption not stated in the sampled text (tg_match_tiebreak): a tiebreak counts as one game so a 7-6 set contributes 13 games, and a deciding-set 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 would contribute the same; an advantage deciding set can produce 20+ games and has no cap.

Strikes in this archetype sit at very different levels (26.5 WTA, 28.5 and 32.5 ATP); the rung is only meaningful relative to the match's format (best-of-three versus best-of-five) which is not part of the strike.

Total sets (KXATPTOTALSETS) is now filed here: 'over 4.5 sets' in best-of-five is exactly the 2-2 path, driven by ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge and ten.within_match_dependence; a retirement at 2-1 or during set 4 is not covered by the visible text, and a set that started but was not completed may or may not count as played.
contract.settlement_data_source: Governing-league recorded set scores summed to completed games; the sampled rules text does not name a vendor or a webpage.

mechanism.summary: Total games is a sum of games across sets, and it is controlled by two things that move in opposite directions: how many sets are played, and how many games each set takes. A mismatched pair produces short sets (6-1, 6-2) and few sets, so totals fall; an evenly matched pair of big servers produces tiebreak sets (13 games) and decider sets, so totals rise. Hold levels set the games-per-set distribution through a discrete mixture of set scores (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 games), while closeness sets the set count, and format caps both. The two are correlated: a match that goes the distance does so because the sets were close, which also lengthens each set, so the joint distribution is heavier-tailed than a product. The contract adds a truncation layer where completed games before retirement are counted, so the over side can settle early and the under side cannot.

stages.name: Format ceiling and final-set rule
stages.description: Format defines the minimum and maximum number of games: a best-of-three runs from 12 games (two bagels) to 39 or more, a best-of-five from 18 to 65 and above. The final-set rule (tiebreak at 6-6, at 12-12, or advantage set) determines whether the right tail is bounded, so the format is a total-count envelope within which the probability mass is placed.
stages.distribution: Deterministic support with a bounded or unbounded right tail depending on the deciding rule; advantage sets create a geometric tail.

stages.name: Pair closeness and the set-count distribution
stages.description: The number of sets played depends on how close the pair is: an even pair reaches a decider about 40-50% of the time, a mismatched pair under 20%. Each additional set adds 8-13 games to the total, so the set count is the largest single lever on the total.
stages.distribution: Discrete 2 or 3 sets in bo3, 3 to 5 in bo5; probability of the long branch is a smooth sigmoid in the rating gap.

stages.name: Games per set from the two hold rates
stages.description: Within a set, each service game is held with probability near 0.6-0.9, and the set score distribution follows: high holds on both sides produce 6-4, 7-5 and 7-6 sets (10-13 games), low holds produce more breaks and 6-2/6-3 sets. This is a mixture over the set score classes, and the discrete masses at 12 and 13 games are what move totals across half-point strikes.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over {6,7,8,9,10,12,13} games per set; the mass at 12-13 games rises sharply with both holds above about 0.8.

stages.name: Lopsided-set tail and style effects
stages.description: Some players produce bagels and breadsticks disproportionately, and strong returners shorten sets by creating breaks while rallying styles lengthen them. These factors act on the lower tail of games per set (6 or 7 games) and on the survival of long sets.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated lower tail on set length; player-specific frequencies around 3-10% of sets with 6-0 or 6-1.

stages.name: Event and condition modifiers on hold levels
stages.description: Court pace, altitude, indoor air and ball type shift every hold probability up or down together, which moves the games per set and tiebreak share for both players at once. Night or day, roof state and wind are the situational layers; these shifts are shared across all matches at an event, so the event's past hold percentage is more informative than the surface label.
stages.distribution: Event-level location shift of several points of hold probability, correlated across matches in the same event and week.

stages.name: Truncation by retirement and the counted-games clause
stages.description: If a player retires, the games completed so far count and the incomplete game does not. The over side of a rung that is already crossed can be settled, but under rungs wait for completion; the probability and timing of retirement therefore asymmetrically affects the two sides of the strike.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event with timing; the completed-games count at retirement is usually about 12-25 in a bo3.

role_personnel.note: A games total is generated by two fixed singles players; there is no lineup, rotation or usage allocation, and a substitution voids to fair price before play.

availability_news.note: Pre-match fitness and withdrawal signals raise the retirement share and shorten matches (both settle-relevant for over rungs); retirement_base_rate and retirement_games_completed_profile size and time the truncation.

coaching_scheme.note: No observable coaching or tactical variable predicts games count at the match level; style effects appear in the return and rally profile rather than in coaching.

ten.games_per_set_distribution.label: Games-per-set distribution from the pair's hold rates
ten.games_per_set_distribution.mechanism: The mass over {6,7,8,9,10,12,13} games for a set is a function of the two hold probabilities.
ten.games_per_set_distribution.rationale: Totals are most sensitive to the discrete masses at 12 and 13 games, which a continuous model misses and which depend on the hold levels in a nonlinear way.
ten.games_per_set_distribution.measurement: For hold probabilities h_A and h_B from adjusted serve/return (A and B alternating serve, first server randomised), compute by dynamic programming the set-score PMF over 6-0 .. 7-6; calibrate to the empirical frequency of set scores from Sackmann by bins of (h_A+h_B)/2 and |h_A-h_B| with kernel smoothing and shrinkage n/(n+60) to the model PMF. Output the PMF of games per set and P(tiebreak). As-of: serve statistics before the match.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings and serve counts
ten.games_per_set_distribution.why: Represents the 12-13 game masses that drive half-point strikes.

ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.label: Completed games at retirement
ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.mechanism: The count of games completed when a retirement ends the match.
ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.rationale: Totals markets settle on completed games, so an interrupted match gives a truncated count; the over side can be settled if the count already exceeds the strike.
ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.measurement: From Sackmann score strings with RET compute games completed by tour and best_of; fit a distribution with covariates (age, round, heat flag) and shrink with n/(n+30); output P(count>k | retirement) for each strike k.
ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.why: Sizes the asymmetric retirement effect on the two sides of a total strike.

ten.player_games_residual.label: Player persistent games-per-match residual
ten.player_games_residual.mechanism: A player's matches end up longer or shorter than a rating-based model predicts, persistently across opponents.
ten.player_games_residual.rationale: Style traits (patient baseline play vs aggressive first-strike tennis) show up as residual match length beyond hold and rating; the existing return-style input is a descriptive profile, not a measured residual.
ten.player_games_residual.measurement: Compute residual_i = games in match minus model expectation (from adjusted hold rates), averaged over the last 40 matches with half-life 9 months, shrunk with n/(n+20) toward 0; test persistence by split-sample correlation before use. As-of date: day before match.
raw_data: adjusted hold rates as-of each match
ten.player_games_residual.why: Captures stable length tendencies not explained by hold rates; usability is subject to a persistence test.

ten.decider_format_tail.label: Deciding-set format and tail probability
ten.decider_format_tail.mechanism: The deciding set can end at 6-6 with a 7-point tiebreak, at 6-6 with a 10-point tiebreak, at 12-12, or only by a two-game margin.
ten.decider_format_tail.rationale: The right tail of totals depends on the final-set rule by event and year; Davis Cup and some tour events differ from the majors.
ten.decider_format_tail.measurement: Event-year lookup of deciding rule; probability of a deciding set exceeding 13 games from the DP model under that rule (0 for tiebreak at 6-6, geometric for advantage sets). Include the format effective date. As-of: official rulebook for the event year.
ten.decider_format_tail.why: Controls how heavy the right tail is for any 'over' strike beyond 30 games.

ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.label: Set-count distribution by edge and format
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.mechanism: The probability mass over 2/3 sets (bo3) or 3/4/5 sets (bo5) as a function of pair edge, surface and tour.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.rationale: Total sets and set spread contracts are direct functions of this distribution; 'any set' is its straight-set complement. The existing catalog lists match length in games but not the set-count distribution.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.measurement: For each completed match (retirements excluded) compute pre-match Elo win prob p from ratings through the prior day. Bin p in 5-point bins by tour x best_of x surface; empirical P(N sets) per bin, fitted by a monotone logistic in logit(p); shrink bin value toward the fit with weight n/(n+40) (no separate additive shrink). Output P(decider), P(straight sets), P(winner dropped a set) per format, walk-forward only.
ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge.why: Shared definition with set_winner_and_any_set; gives P(decider) and P(straight sets) by edge and format, which set the number of sets (the largest lever on the games total) and the rungs of KXATPTOTALSETS.

ten.hold_break.reason: The mechanism behind games per set, but only its distributional form (the PMF) matters for totals, so define the PMF explicitly.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Rating gap drives set count; a closeness measure is the real input, so keep as the base from which closeness is computed.

ten.format.reason: Fixes the count envelope; a bo3 strike read as bo5 is a total error.

ten.final_set_rule.reason: The final-set rule and the deciding-set tail are the same fact; keep the new definition which includes the tail probability and effective date.

ten.tiebreak_reach_probability.reason: The 13-game outcome is the largest discrete jump in the total; central, but derived from hold probabilities.

ten.lopsided_set_rate.reason: Explains the lower tail beyond the average rating gap; useful but small sample per player.

ten.venue_speed_history.reason: Event-level hold history is the best environment proxy for games per set; shared across all matches at the event.

ten.retirement_base_rate.reason: Frequency alone is not enough because the asymmetric settlement depends on the count at retirement, which the new profile provides.

ten.retirement_settlement_rules.reason: Clause truncated in the sample; the settlement of the under side after a retirement is unobserved.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Its catalog measurement fits a distribution to Kalshi mid prices across rungs and reports an implied PMF, so it is market-derived: useful only to benchmark and sanity-check model rung probabilities (monotonicity, sum-to-one), never as an outcome input or a coverage claim.

ten.serve_return.reason: Raw spw/rpw are the ingredients of hold; hold_break already carries them and listing both double counts.

ten.tiebreak.reason: A tiebreak always contributes exactly one game after 12, so win rate affects set winner not games total; irrelevant for totals beyond its occurrence.

ten.schedule.reason: The claim that night sessions raise totals is unsupported (cooler air slows balls); only roof state or indoor flag is decisive, and that sits in the venue and condition inputs.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realised frequency by strike is a market-calibration table, not a determinant of games played; benchmark only.

ten.return_style_rally.reason: Return aggression and rally length shape break frequency; mostly captured by hold rates.

ten.match_length_expectation.reason: Expected service games per set sets the tiebreak and straight-set exposure and is the input used by the aces, spreads and exact-score records; the games-per-set PMF carries more information for this total, so it is secondary here rather than a duplicate, which also removes the verdict inconsistency across tennis records.

ten.first_serve.reason: First-serve in% and points won drive holds; overlaps adjusted serve rates but useful as a decomposition.

ten.break_point_luck.reason: Season-scale regression of break-point conversion has small effect on one match's total once holds are measured.

interactions.mechanism: Closeness raises set count while high holds raise games per set; the two co-move because close matches between holders produce long sets and a decider, so the joint distribution has a heavier right tail than their product.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the simulated P(total>k) from independent set-count and per-set distributions with one using the joint model, against historical frequencies.

interactions.mechanism: The effect of the deciding-set rule depends on format: in best-of-five an advantage set can add many games to the total, whereas in best-of-three the same rule matters only in a third set.
interactions.how_to_test: Split totals above 40 games by final-set rule and format and compare tail frequencies.

interactions.mechanism: Faster events push both holds up, and tiebreak probability rises faster than linearly with hold; the shift in expected games per set is largest between the middle and top of the pace distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress P(tiebreak per set) on event hold% and test a quadratic term.

interactions.mechanism: Once games completed exceeds the strike, a retirement settles Yes; below it the market waits, so the retirement hazard acts differently across rungs depending on how many games have been played.
interactions.how_to_test: Enumerate historical retirement matches and compute which strikes would have been settled by games completed.

interactions.mechanism: A player who often wins 6-1 sets and a returner who breaks frequently compound in short sets; the combined effect on totals saturates because the minimum games per set is 6.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare totals in matches pairing a high lopsided-rate player and strong returner against the additive prediction.

interactions.mechanism: A shared day-level form shock makes close sets cluster: it raises the probability of a decider and of long tiebreak sets together, so set count and games per set are positively dependent beyond what the two marginals imply, widening the total's variance and fattening its right tail on every over-rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the variance of games totals in historical matches with the variance implied by independent set draws at the same edge bins; test whether the excess variance rises with the within-match dependence estimate.

nonlinearities.why: The 13-game mass grows rapidly as both holds exceed 0.8, so the total's survival function above 24.5 is far more sensitive to hold than the mean games per set.
A tiebreak at 6-6 caps the deciding set at 13 games whereas advantage rules allow 20+, a regime difference that changes probabilities of strikes above about 40 games.
The probability of a third set drops from near 50% for even pairs to under 20% for large gaps; the transition is steepest in the middle where a small rating error changes the total by about a set.

contract.settlement_definition: Seventeen live series; all but KXATPMEN (title only) now have rules text. Outright winners: KXATP and KXWTA ('If Matteo Berrettini wins the 2026 ATP Paris professional tennis tournament') resolve No for a participant who 'forfeits, withdraws from consideration, or takes any official action that removes them from being able to win'; KXATPFINALS, KXWTAFINALS and KXATPNEXTGEN have only a primary sentence. Round-winner series (KXATPIWO, KXATPIT, KXWTAIT, KXATPMCO, KXWTAMOA, KXWTAATX; archived 2025 markets) settle on the player being 'a winner of the final/quarterfinal' of the event, i.e. winning that round (for a final, the title; otherwise equivalent to reaching the next stage). Stage contracts KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE settle Yes on qualifying for the Final 'if they qualify but do not end up competing'. KXWTAROE settles on the exact round of elimination, with a withdrawal assigned to the next stage the player would have been eliminated in. KXATPSETSWEEP requires winning the tournament while winning 'every completed set they play'; retirement, walkover, default or disqualification follow official advancement and scoring records. KXWTATOURNWIN settles Yes if the named player wins any WTA tournament, singles or doubles, in 2026. Not stated: lucky-loser replacement, a final decided by walkover for the outright, and the source of truth.

variants_and_edge_cases: Round-robin finals (ATP Finals, WTA Finals, Next Gen Finals): a group stage with qualification to semifinals by wins, then by head-to-head, set ratio and game ratio, plus alternates replacing withdrawn players; the structure differs from a knockout bracket.

Withdrawal asymmetry: outright winners settle No if the participant withdraws (KXATP, KXWTA), stage contracts settle Yes if the player qualified for the Final but does not compete (KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE), and KXWTAROE assigns a withdrawing player the next elimination stage; the same withdrawal moves the three contract types differently.

Tournament sweep (KXATPSETSWEEP): Yes needs the title plus every completed set won; an opponent retiring mid-set leaves the unfinished set uncounted, while a walkover adds a round with no sets, so retirements and walkovers raise the sweep probability relative to a full-play model.

Round-winner series (KXATPIWO, KXATPIT, KXWTAIT, KXATPMCO, KXWTAMOA, KXWTAATX) and the identical tournament-named series filed under match_winner (KXATPMAD, KXWTAIWO ...) are the same object; listing time relative to the draw is not stated.

KXWTATOURNWIN names players who may not be active (sample: Serena Williams); for them the event is gated by a return to competition, and doubles titles count, which is a different path from singles strength.
Season finals and Next Gen winner series (KXATPFINALS, KXWTAFINALS, KXATPNEXTGEN) have only a primary sentence; their withdrawal and alternate treatment is not stated.
