mechanism.summary: A tournament outcome is a path product across a bracket: to win, a player must be in the field, avoid injury, and win about six or seven consecutive matches against opponents determined by a draw that is random subject to seeding. Before the draw is published the probability averages over draw randomness, flattening the favourite; after the draw it is conditional on the actual path. Within an event the path is not independent across rounds, since fatigue accumulates, injuries occur, in-tournament form updates, and withdrawals reshuffle the bracket, and across players in the same half the outcomes are coupled because one player's win removes another's path. Round-robin finals and team formats replace the path product with a group structure and tie-break rules. The settlement layer adds a distinct feature: for stage contracts a player who qualifies but does not play the final still pays, so withdrawal timing matters differently by stage.

stages.name: Field formation: entry, withdrawals and replacement
stages.description: The field is determined by entry lists, withdrawals before and after the draw, and replacement by alternates and lucky losers. A top player's absence removes the main competitor for everyone else and changes the bracket. Withdrawals concentrate among players with injury layoffs and are timestamped in a way that matters to price.
stages.distribution: Discrete field composition with a withdrawal hazard concentrated close to the draw and first match; clustered in injured and older players.

stages.name: Draw structure and seeding
stages.description: Seeding rules separate the top seeds into different quarters, so a seed's expected opponent strength in early rounds is determined by those rules. Before the draw the model averages over random placement conditional on seeding; after it, the actual bracket sets each player's path difficulty and potential meetings. Round-robin finals replace this with group composition.
stages.distribution: Combinatorial distribution of brackets under seeding constraints; heterogeneity in path difficulty is large for players seeded 5-8.

stages.name: Match-level win probabilities with uncertainty
stages.description: Each match on the path has a win probability from surface-adjusted ratings at the event's pace, with honest uncertainty. Rating uncertainty flattens favourites and matters because a title is the product of six or seven probabilities, so small per-match errors compound.
stages.distribution: Product of 6-7 Bernoulli probabilities; relative error of the product is about the sum of relative errors per match.

stages.name: Path dependence: fatigue, in-event updating and injury
stages.description: Long early matches cost later performance, and in-event results update the ratings (a player playing at a high level through four rounds is more likely to continue). Qualifiers and lucky losers carry a different load profile. Injury risk accumulates across rounds and in best-of-five formats.
stages.distribution: Positively correlated successive match outcomes; fatigue effects are small per round but compound over seven rounds.

stages.name: Dependence within the draw and nationality coupling
stages.description: Players in the same half cannot both reach the final, so their outcomes are negatively dependent; upset shocks shared across top seeds create positive dependence among their early losses. For the stage contracts (KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE) two players in the same half are mutually exclusive finalists, and for KXWTAROE one player's elimination round fixes the opponent's next round.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution with negative dependence within halves and positive dependence in shared shocks; covariance depends on bracket positions.

stages.name: Settlement of outright and stage contracts
stages.description: Outright-winner contracts settle No for a participant who withdraws or is removed, while stage contracts settle Yes once the player qualifies for the Final even if he does not compete; the same withdrawal therefore has opposite payoffs by contract type. For season-finals winner contracts listed before the field is set, the remaining race decides who is in the field, so race arithmetic enters only as field formation context. Round-winner series settle on winning the named round (the title when the round is the final), and KXWTAROE needs the full PMF of the elimination round, P(reach r) - P(reach r+1), with a withdrawal after a win assigned to the next round, so in-event withdrawal hazard shifts mass one round later instead of to No.
stages.distribution: Point mass on settlement at qualification or withdrawal events; a Bernoulli withdrawal hazard whose payoff sign depends on contract type.

stages.name: Tournament set-drop path for the no-dropped-set title
stages.description: KXATPSETSWEEP pays only if the named player wins the title and wins every completed set. Per round this is P(win) times P(straight sets | win) against the round's opponent distribution, and the title-level probability is the product over rounds with a shared form shock that makes clean early rounds predictive of clean later ones. Best-of-five Slams require seven 3-0 wins, so the event is far rarer than the title and concentrated on dominant servers with a low set-drop propensity; walkovers and opponent retirements before a completed set count in the player's favour under the completed-set rule.
stages.distribution: Product of round-level Bernoulli probabilities with positive dependence; heavy concentration at near zero for all but one or two players; extremely sensitive to the straight-set conversion curve at high edges.

stages.name: Return-gated any-event title for inactive players
stages.description: KXWTATOURNWIN asks whether a named player wins any WTA tournament, singles or doubles, within 2026; the sample names a retired player. The probability is P(returns to competition in time) times P(at least one title over the events entered), where the second factor is a union over a short schedule and doubles events offer an easier path (smaller fields, partner choice). For an active player it reduces to a calendar union of title probabilities with health-linked dependence across events.
stages.distribution: Mixture of a point mass at zero (no return) and a union over a few events with small per-event probabilities; positively dependent through form and health; doubles adds a separate path.

coaching_scheme.note: No coaching or tactical variable is observable at tournament-path scale; effects pass through ratings and form, and there is no separate coaching quantity to forecast.

pace_volume.note: A tournament contract has no volume count; the number of rounds is fixed by the draw size and format and is not a forecast quantity.

ten.round_robin_group_structure.label: Round-robin group structure and tie-break rules
ten.round_robin_group_structure.mechanism: In round-robin finals, advancement depends on group composition, results and tie-break rules, not on a knockout path.
ten.round_robin_group_structure.rationale: ATP Finals, WTA Finals and Next Gen Finals use groups; the probability of advancing is a function of the three-match group and tie-break rules (wins, head-to-head, set ratio, game ratio), and alternates replace withdrawals.
ten.round_robin_group_structure.measurement: Simulate each group of four: 6 matches in total (3 per player) with win probability from indoor-hard pace-adjusted ratings, set scores sampled from the set-count distribution, games from the game-margin pmf. Rank by wins, then head-to-head (two tied), then set ratio, then game ratio per the rulebook of that year (multi-way tie rule coded). P(advance)=top two of group; P(title)=P(advance) x semifinal x final win probabilities from the knockout sim. Withdrawals replaced by next alternate per rulebook with prob from withdrawal hazard. As-of: group draw.
raw_data: group composition, tie-break rules by year, results
ten.round_robin_group_structure.why: The knockout path model is invalid for groups; this input holds the group-specific structure.

ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.label: Withdrawal cascade through the bracket
ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.mechanism: A withdrawal changes the bracket: the opponent gets a walkover (rest), a lucky loser enters, and the path of other players shifts.
ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.rationale: The stage rule says a player who qualifies for the final but does not play still pays, so withdrawals at different points settle differently, and a withdrawal reshuffles the title probabilities of everyone else.
ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.measurement: For each possible withdrawal, recompute title and stage probabilities with the replacement rules (lucky loser from qualifying draw with ratings, opponent's walkover with rest credit); weight by an empirical day-level withdrawal rate by round taken from W/O score rows (no timestamp; see tw_withdrawal_vintage and tw_sackmann_access), and treat any horizon-specific weighting as available only from forward own-capture; output the sensitivity of each player's title probability to the top-8 players' withdrawals.
ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.why: Models the mechanism by which a withdrawal propagates to prices of all other players.

ten.round_upset_calibration.label: Round-by-round upset calibration by seed band
ten.round_upset_calibration.mechanism: Empirical upset frequency by round, seed band and surface to calibrate the path simulation.
ten.round_upset_calibration.rationale: A model that multiplies match probabilities can be miscalibrated for early-round upsets and late-round parity; the calibration table is a data-driven check.
ten.round_upset_calibration.measurement: From Sackmann results compute by round and seed-difference bin the favourite's win frequency relative to the Elo-implied probability; fit a logistic correction with round dummies; shrink to 0 with n/(n+100); apply to the simulation. As-of: before event.
raw_data: match rows with seed and round
ten.round_upset_calibration.why: Provides the empirical correction that the product-of-probabilities model lacks.

ten.in_event_rating_update.label: In-event rating and form updating
ten.in_event_rating_update.mechanism: As a tournament proceeds, each round's performance (serve and return numbers, not just win/loss) updates a player's strength estimate.
ten.in_event_rating_update.rationale: The title probability before round four should use information from rounds one to three; a dominant straight-set run is evidence about current form and health that pre-event ratings do not have.
ten.in_event_rating_update.measurement: dominance_m = (points won by player) / (total points) from match stats (Sackmann w_/l_ columns if present, else games won / games played). expected_m = pre-match expected points share from Elo (convert Elo win prob to points share via the fitted monotone map on history). resid_m = dominance_m - expected_m. Next-round Elo adjustment = clip(k * 400/ln10 * sum_m decay_m * resid_m, -40, 40) with k=0.15, decay_m = 1 - days_since/10 (0 beyond 10 days). k, clip, decay are placeholders to fit by out-of-sample log loss. As-of: after each completed match.
free_sources: Sackmann CSV (serve stats by match, when available)
raw_data: per-round match serve and return statistics
ten.in_event_rating_update.why: Introduces information that arrives during the event for futures contracts that stay open until the final.

ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.label: Remaining-points arithmetic to the snapshot date
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.mechanism: Maximum and minimum achievable ranking points by the settlement date for each contender, given drop-offs and remaining events. The same race arithmetic also settles Finals-qualification contracts (cutoff at the 8th place, alternates).
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.rationale: In early November the rank is almost mechanically bounded; probability of overtaking is zero unless the gap is less than the maximum swing, and nonzero only through a small set of events.
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.measurement: For each player compute P_end = P_now - drop(t..T) + sum over remaining events of earned points; maximum earned by event structure (for example Finals: 200 per round-robin win, 400 semifinal, 500 final, 1500 undefeated; Masters 1000 etc.); minimum from not playing; compute the probability of rank 1 (or top 5) by simulation constrained by these bounds; update after each event. As-of: after each Monday publication. Finals qualification (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL; title only): qualifier count is eight singles places, the cutoff is the 8th-place Race to the Finals total at the qualification date, a withdrawn qualifier is replaced by the next alternate in race order, and the probability of qualifying is the simulated probability of finishing in the top eight after applying participation hazards; special exemptions (for example the treatment of Grand Slam winners outside the top eight) and doubles-team qualification are not modelled and are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (sr_finals_qual_contracts).
raw_data: current points, expiry schedule, points table, remaining calendar
ten.remaining_race_arithmetic.why: Context only after the reconciliation: decides which players form the ATP/WTA Finals and Next Gen fields before they are fixed (relevant to KXATPFINALS/KXWTAFINALS winner prices quoted early); the Finals-qualification series themselves now live in season_ranking_and_majors, which owns this definition.

ten.short_format_rules.label: Next Gen Finals short-format scoring rules
ten.short_format_rules.mechanism: Short sets (first to four games, tiebreak at 3-3), no-ad scoring and a best-of-five sets match change the point-to-match map, so favourite probabilities and round-robin set/game ratios differ from standard best-of-three tour matches.
ten.short_format_rules.rationale: KXATPNEXTGEN is a live series and the Next Gen Finals use a shortened format; applying standard-set hold-to-match conversion misstates match win probability and the set/game-ratio tiebreaks that decide round-robin advancement.
ten.short_format_rules.measurement: Code the event format from the current-year rulebook (sets to win, games per set, tiebreak score, ad or no-ad, let rule). Convert spw to the game hold probability with the no-ad formula (the receiver wins the single deciding point at 3-3, so hold = sum over scores of the point-win probabilities with one deciding point), then to a first-to-four set with a tiebreak at 3-3 by a DP over game scores, then to best-of-five sets. Use per-player spw/rpw with a short-format variance inflation estimated from past Next Gen Finals sets (pooled shrinkage n/(n+40) toward the standard-format model). As-of: rulebook publication before the event; rules change between years so the year is part of the key.
free_sources: ATP Next Gen Finals rulebook and event page
Wikipedia event pages for past editions
raw_data: past Next Gen Finals set/game scores
ten.short_format_rules.why: The live series KXATPNEXTGEN (Next Gen Finals) uses a shortened format that needs a different match and round-robin map than the standard model; without this input the series has no format coding.

ten.path_difficulty_sim.reason: A Monte Carlo over draw, ratings, fatigue and withdrawals is the model that consumes the inputs, not an input; kept as the aggregation engine whose ingredients (draw, surface_rating, rating_uncertainty, pre_draw_field) carry the primary roles.

ten.draw.reason: The bracket, seeding positions and order of play are the required raw data for every path-dependent contract; they are measured, not modelled, and are the input to the simulation rather than a duplicate of it.

ten.surface_rating.reason: Match-level strength; needs pace-sensitive and best-of-five aware adjustments for the event.

ten.venue_speed_history.reason: Event pace changes who is favoured and the variance of outcomes; stable across editions.

ten.pre_draw_field.reason: Field composition before the draw drives the outright probabilities; needs timestamped snapshots.

ten.bracket_correlation.reason: Dependence among players is an output of the joint simulation over the draw, not a measured input; kept as a diagnostic and removed from interaction inputs in favour of the draw itself.

ten.fatigue.reason: Accumulated load matters through minutes and sets in prior rounds; small per round, compounds across the path.

ten.fitness.reason: Injury and withdrawal probability is the largest source of field uncertainty for top players.

ten.rating_uncertainty.reason: Flattens favourites in a product of six or seven probabilities; implemented as sampling error in the simulation.

ten.round_context.reason: Round and seeding are outputs of the draw rather than separate information; the seed itself is useful for upset calibration only.

m.rules_text.reason: The 'qualifies but does not compete still pays' rule changes withdrawal value; read per series.

ten.form.reason: Recent form double counts rating updates; in-event updating is a more specific definition.

ten.motivation.reason: Event priority matters for non-majors where top players rest or tank; hard to quantify.

ten.schedule.reason: Order of play and delays shift rest by hours; relevant in the later rounds but small.

ten.travel_timezone.reason: Largest in early rounds after intercontinental travel; small for later rounds.

ten.qualifying_path_fatigue.reason: Qualifiers play extra matches; a small effect once in the main draw, material for lucky-loser entrants.

interactions.mechanism: A title is a product of six or seven match probabilities, so relative errors compound multiplicatively; a favourite's rating uncertainty therefore lowers title probability by more than it lowers a single match probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare title probabilities from simulations with point-estimate ratings versus ratings sampled from posteriors, and check calibration across past events.

interactions.mechanism: A withdrawal before the draw changes seeding and who is placed where, whereas after the draw it changes only a path; the effects on other players differ by regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare title probability shifts of other seeds when a top player withdraws before and after the draw.

interactions.mechanism: In a round-robin group, a player can lose a match and still advance, so rating differences translate into advancement more weakly than into a knockout round; tie-break rules (sets ratio) add sensitivity to margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate groups with identical ratings under knockout versus group rules and compare advancement probabilities.

interactions.mechanism: A long early match lowers later performance but may also reveal strong form; the net effect depends on whether the player won efficiently, which is a conditional relationship.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress later-round win probability on prior match minutes interacted with dominance ratio.

interactions.mechanism: Next Gen first-to-four sets with no-ad games cut the points per match, so a given rating gap converts into a smaller match-win edge and rating error matters relatively less than format noise; the favourite's title probability in KXATPNEXTGEN is flatter than a best-of-three model with the same ratings would give, and the flattening is conditional on the short format.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare favourite win rates by Elo-gap bin in Next Gen Finals (short sets, no-ad) against best-of-three tour matches with the same gaps; a smaller slope in the short format confirms the conditional compression.

nonlinearities.why: Title probability is a product of round-by-round probabilities, so a one-point change in per-match win probability has a larger relative effect on the title for a longer path than a shorter one.

Posterior uncertainty in rating reduces the title probability of the strongest player and raises the longshots' probability in a nonlinear fashion because the title is a tail of the product distribution.
Fatigue shows up only after a high cumulative load (for example more than about 12 hours on court over five rounds in a Slam), then the penalty grows; below that it is negligible.
